value.zh: 遺榮參日月，百世仰餘暉。
value.en: Yielding fame they match luminaries—centuries lift eyes to lingering glow.
value.literal: Renouncing glory they rival sun and moon—hundred ages gaze up at afterglow.

value.zh: 宗親會歌張華
value.en: Lineage Gathering Hymn—Zhang Hua
value.literal: Song for Clan Kinsmen Assembly—by Zhang Hua

value.zh: 泰始九年，光祿大夫荀勖以杜夔所制律呂，校太樂、總章、鼓吹八音，與律呂乖錯，乃制古尺，作新律呂，以調聲韻。
value.en: the ninth year of Taishi saw Xun Xu compare Du Kui’s pitch system with palace ensembles and martial bands; finding mismatch, he cast archaic rods and new tubes to true the scale.
value.literal: In the ninth year of Taishi, Minister Guanglu Xun Xu, because the pitch pipes Du Kui had devised—when checked against Grand Music, General Regulation, and Drum-and-Bugle eight timbres—clashed with standard lu, then fashioned ancient foot-rules and cast new pitch tubes to tune modes and intervals.

value.zh: 事具《律曆志》。
value.en: Full detail appears in the treatise on harmonics and calendrics.
value.literal: The matter is fully recorded in the “Treatise on Pitch Pipes and the Calendar.”

value.zh: 律成，遂班下太常，使太樂、總章、鼓吹、清商施用。
value.en: Once the pitch-pipes were complete, they were promulgated to the Chamberlain of Ceremonial for Grand Music, General Regulation, Drum-and-Bugle, and Pure Shop to adopt them.
value.literal: Once the pipes were complete, orders went down to the Chamberlain of Ceremonial for Grand Music, General Regulation, Drum-and-Bugle, and Pure Shop to adopt them.

value.zh: 勖遂典知樂事，啟朝士解音律者共掌之。
value.en: Xun Xu took charge of performance and asked literati who understood temperament to co-manage it.
value.literal: Xun Xu then supervised musical affairs and memorialized that court gentlemen who grasped pitch theory should jointly administer them.

value.zh: 使郭夏、宋識等造《正德》、《大豫》二舞，其樂章亦張華之所作雲。
value.en: He tasked Guo Xia and Song Shi with choreography for “Zhengde” and “Dayu”—lyrics again from Zhang Hua.
value.literal: He assigned Guo Xia, Song Shi, and others to create the two dances “Correct Virtue” and “Grand Ease”—their lyrics likewise composed by Zhang Hua.

value.zh: 正德舞歌張華
value.en: “Zhengde” Dance Hymn—Zhang Hua
value.literal: Correct Virtue Dance Song—by Zhang Hua

value.zh: 日皇上天，玄鑒惟光。
value.en: Solar lord aloft—shadowy scrutiny alone shines.
value.literal: Sun august, Heaven high—dark mirror alone sheds light.

value.zh: 神器周回，五德代章。
value.en: Divine tokens wheel—five virtues take rotating glory.
value.literal: Sacred regalia cycles round—five powers replace in splendor.

value.zh: 祚命于晉，世有哲王。
value.en: Heaven’s lot settles on Jin—successions seat sagely rulers.
value.literal: Fortune’s mandate rests with Jin—ages hold wise kings.

value.zh: 弘濟區夏，陶甄萬方。
value.en: They rescue central plain—they kiln-fire every quarter.
value.literal: They broadly succor inner summer—they mold and fire myriad directions.

value.zh: 大明垂曜，旁燭無疆。
value.en: Grand splendor lowers gleam—peripheral torches know no bound.
value.literal: Great brilliance hangs its glow—side lamps illumine without limit.

value.zh: 蚩蚩庶類，風德永康。
value.en: Teeming common folk—custom’s power ever robust.
value.literal: Busy busy common kinds—wind virtue forever strong.

value.zh: 皇道惟清，禮樂斯經。
value.en: The royal way stays lucid—rites and song form its fixed threads.
value.literal: Imperial path alone is pure—ritual and music are its warp.

value.zh: 金石在懸，萬舞在庭。
value.en: Bronze and jade hang ranked—countless dancers pack the yard.
value.literal: Metal and stone hang suspended—myriad dancers fill courtyard.

value.zh: 象容表慶，協律被聲。
value.en: Figures display fortune—they wed mode and mantle tone.
value.literal: Gestures image blessing—they harmonize pitch and cloak sound.

value.zh: 軼《武》超《濩》，取節《六英》。
value.en: Leaping past “Grand Wu,” vaulting “Grand Hu”—they steal rhythm from “Six Ying.”
value.literal: Surpassing “Wu,” transcending “Hu”—they borrow beat from “Six Ying.”

value.zh: 同進退讓，化漸無形。
value.en: Joint charge, joint retreat—reform trickles past visible form.
value.literal: Together advancing, together yielding—transformation seeps beyond shape.

value.zh: 大和宣洽，通於幽冥。
value.en: Supreme concord spreads—it threads silent shades.
value.literal: Grand harmony proclaimed concord—it penetrates dim netherworld.

value.zh: 大豫舞歌張華
value.en: “Dayu” Dance Hymn—Zhang Hua
value.literal: Grand Ease Dance Song—by Zhang Hua

value.zh: 惟天之命，符運有歸。
value.en: Thus runs celestial writ—omens and luck own their course.
value.literal: Such is Heaven’s command—tally and fortune know their return.

value.zh: 赫赫大晉，三後重暉。
value.en: Resplendent mighty Jin—three successors stacked glory.
value.literal: Blazing Great Jin—three later lords doubled splendor.

value.zh: 繼明紹世，光撫九圍。
value.en: Carrying flame, handing eras—gleam nurses nine peripheries.
value.literal: Continuing brilliance, renewing ages—radiance soothes nine spheres.

value.zh: 我皇紹期，遂在璿璣。
value.en: Our sovereign takes timed mandate—therefore sits on polar hinge.
value.literal: Our emperor inherits destined season—thus rests upon celestial pivot.

value.zh: 群生屬命，奄有庶邦。
value.en: Creatures hang fortunes—swiftly holding myriad states.
value.literal: Myriad lives attach their fate—suddenly possessing hundred domains.

value.zh: 慎徽五典，玄教遐通。
value.en: Guardedly honoring five statutes—arcane doctrine bridges distance.
value.literal: Carefully tracing five canons—dark teaching reaches far.

value.zh: 萬方同軌，率土咸雍。
value.en: Ten thousand regions ride shared gauge—every soil merges ease.
value.literal: Myriad quarters share one track—all soils join harmony.

value.zh: 爰制《大豫》，宣德舞功。
value.en: Hence choreographed “Grand Ease”—spreading merit through swaying ode.
value.literal: Thus they fashioned “Grand Ease”—broadcasting virtue through dance merit.

value.zh: 醇化既穆，王道協隆。
value.en: Distilled reform stands grave—royal course aligns with height.
value.literal: Pure transformation already solemn—kingly Way coordinated lofty.

value.zh: 仁及草木，惠加昆蟲。
value.en: Mercy touches herb and timber—bounty sinks to creeping kin.
value.literal: Kindness reaches grass and trees—grace adds even to crawling things.

value.zh: 億兆夷人，悅仰皇風。
value.en: Countless tribes beyond heartland—gladly crane toward sovereign wind.
value.literal: Hundred millions of barbarian folk—joyfully lift eyes to royal breeze.

value.zh: 丕顯大業，永世彌崇。
value.en: Brightly shown mega-work—endless reigns heap reverence.
value.literal: Brilliantly manifest great enterprise—forever ages it mounts revered.

value.zh: 言之不從，是謂不乂
value.en: When commands find no compliance, the canon calls it a failure of proper order.
value.literal: When commands find no compliance, the canon calls it a failure of proper order.

value.zh: 永康元年四月，立皇孫臧為皇太孫。
value.en: In the first year of Yongkang, Sima Zang became heir-apparent.
value.literal: In the first year of Yongkang, fourth month — imperial grandson Zang was made heir.

value.zh: 五月甲子，就東宮，桑又生於西廂。
value.en: The mulberry returned when Zang entered.
value.literal: Fifth month jiazi — entering the Eastern Palace mulberry again grew in the west wing.

value.zh: 明年，趙王倫篡位，鴆殺臧，此與湣懷同妖也。
value.en: Lun's coup killed Zang like earlier heirs.
value.literal: Next year Prince Zhao Lun usurped and poisoned Zang — same portent as Min and Huai.

value.zh: 是月，壯武國有桑化為柏，而張華遇害。
value.en: Mulberry-cypress shift coincided with Zhang Hua's death.
value.literal: That month Zhuangwu princedom saw mulberry turn to cypress while Zhang Hua was murdered.

value.zh: 壯武，華之封邑也。
value.en: The omen struck his domain.
value.literal: Zhuangwu was Hua's fief.

value.zh: 刑法志
value.en: Monograph: Criminal Law.
value.literal: Treatise on Punishment and Law.

value.zh: 是時侍中盧珽、中書侍郎張華又表：「抄《新律》諸死罪條目，懸之亭傳，以示兆庶。」
value.en: At this time Attendant Lu Ting and Palace Writer Attendant Gentleman Zhang Hua again memorialized: "Copy out the articles for the capital crimes in the New Code and hang them in stations and relay posts to show them to the common people."
value.literal: At this time Attendant Lu Ting and Palace Writer Attendant Gentleman Zhang Hua again memorialized: "Copy out the articles for the capital crimes in the New Code and hang them in stations and relay posts to show them to the common people."

value.zh: 有詔從之。
value.en: The throne agreed.
value.literal: An edict approved.

value.zh: 夫乾坤定位，男女流形，伉儷之義同歸，貴賤之名異等。
value.en: Heaven and earth fixed their stations; men and women took their bodily shapes. Husband and wife share one moral purpose, even though rank divides high from low.
value.literal: As for Qian and Kun taking their positions, male and female receive their forms; the principle of husband and wife aims at the same end, yet the names of noble and base stand in different ranks.

value.zh: 若乃作配皇極，齊體紫宸，象玉床之連後星，喻金波之合羲璧。
value.en: Those who match the sovereign on high and share the body politic of the inner palace are figured as the jade couch tied to the queen’s asterism, as moonlight married to the solar disk.
value.literal: When one is paired with the supreme apex and shares the substance of the Purple Palace, it is likened to the jade couch linking to the rear stars, and compared to golden waves joining the Xi disk.

value.zh: 爰自敻古，是謂元妃；
value.en: In deepest antiquity she was known as the principal wife;
value.literal: From remote antiquity onward, she was called the chief consort;

value.zh: 降及中年，乃稱王后。
value.en: Later ages styled her queen.
value.literal: Descending to middle antiquity, she was then titled queen.

value.zh: 四人並列，光于帝嚳之宮；
value.en: Four consorts stood side by side and brought glory to Emperor Ku’s inner court;
value.literal: Four women stood ranked together, shining in the palace of Emperor Ku;

value.zh: 二妃同降，著彼有虞之典。
value.en: Two royal brides arrived together and entered the canonical record of Shun’s reign.
value.literal: Two consorts descended together, written into the canons of Yu’s age.

value.zh: 夏商以上，六宮之制，其詳靡得而聞焉。
value.en: For ages before Xia and Shang, no reliable detail survives about how the six wings of the harem were ordered.
value.literal: Above Xia and Shang, the regulations of the Six Palaces cannot be heard of in detail.

value.zh: 姬劉以降，五翟之規，其事可略而言矣。
value.en: From the Zhou and Han dynasties on, the graded “five pheasant” ritual for consorts can at least be sketched.
value.literal: From Ji and Liu onward, the rules of the five pheasant insignia may be spoken of in outline.

value.zh: 周禮，天子立一后、三夫人、九嬪、二十七世婦、八十一御妻，以聽王者內政。
value.en: The Rites of Zhou prescribe one empress, three chief consorts, nine ranked ladies, twenty-seven secondary wives, and eighty-one attendants to manage the sovereign’s domestic government.
value.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, the Son of Heaven establishes one queen, three ladies, nine bin, twenty-seven wives of rank, and eighty-one minor wives, to administer the king’s inner administration.

value.zh: 故婚義曰：「天子之與后，如日之與月，陰之與陽。」
value.en: The Meaning of Marriage therefore declares: “The emperor and his empress mirror sun and moon, yin and yang.”
value.literal: Therefore the Meaning of Marriage says: “The Son of Heaven and the queen are like sun and moon, yin and yang.”

value.zh: 由斯而談，其所從來遠矣。
value.en: Judged by such language, their institution reaches far back into antiquity.
value.literal: From this perspective, what they derive from is distant indeed.

value.zh: 故能母儀天宇，助宣王化，德均載物，比大坤維，宗廟歆其薦羞，穹壤俟其交泰。
value.en: Hence she sets the maternal standard for the realm, advances the king’s civilizing work, and bears creation as steadfastly as earth itself; the temple accepts her sacrifices gladly, and heaven and earth look to her union with the throne for peace.
value.literal: Thus she can be the motherly model for all under heaven, aid in spreading royal transformation, her virtue evenly bearing all things, comparable to the great sustaining power of Kun; the ancestral temple delights in her offerings, heaven and earth await her harmonizing union.

value.zh: 是以哲王垂憲，尤重造舟之禮；
value.en: That is why enlightened monarchs codify law and prize above all the royal wedding rite of “meeting across the boat.”
value.literal: Therefore wise kings hang forth statutes and especially esteem the rite of the built bridge;

value.zh: 詩人立言，先獎葛覃之訓。
value.en: The Classic of Poetry opens by honoring the lessons of “Ge Tan,” the ode on diligent royal ladies.
value.literal: The poets set forth words and first praise the instruction of “Ge Tan.”

value.zh: 後燭流景，所以裁其宴私；
value.en: Dimming the late-night lamp curbs excess in the privy chamber;
value.literal: The rear candle’s flowing light is the means to regulate their private banquets;

value.zh: 房樂希聲，是用節其容止。
value.en: Sparse music in the inner rooms reins in conduct at court and couch alike.
value.literal: Chamber music with sparse sound is the means to moderate their bearing.

value.zh: 履端正本，抑斯之謂歟！
value.en: Walking straight to set the root right—surely this is what those measures intend!
value.literal: Walking upright to rectify the root—is this not what is meant!

value.zh: 若乃娉納有方，防閑有禮，肅尊儀而修四德，體柔範而弘六義，陰教洽于宮闈，淑譽騰於區域。
value.en: When matches are arranged by rule, propriety fences passion, majesty guards ritual while the four womanly virtues are cultivated, gentle models enlarge the six canonical lessons, inner-chamber teaching fills the harem, and fair fame spreads beyond the capital.
value.literal: If betrothal and intake have proper method, fences and restraint have ritual, reverently honoring ceremony while cultivating the four virtues, embodying gentle norms while extending the six meanings, then women’s instruction permeates the palace, and good reputation rises through the regions.

value.zh: 則玄雲入戶，上帝錫母萌之符；
value.en: Then auspicious clouds cross the threshold and Heaven grants the token of fruitful motherhood;
value.literal: Then dark clouds enter the door, and the Supreme Lord grants the sign of motherhood’s sprouting;

value.zh: 黃神降徵，坤靈贊壽丘之道，終能鼎祚惟永，胤嗣克昌。
value.en: The divine Yellow Emperor sends portents; earth’s spirit blesses the birth-hill of sage-kings; the dynasty’s mandate endures and heirs thrive.
value.literal: The Yellow Spirit sends down omens; the spirit of Kun assists the way of Shouqiu; ultimately the tripod fortune can be everlasting and heirs flourish.

value.zh: 至若儷極虧閑，憑天作孽，倒裳衣于衽席，感朓側於弦望。
value.en: But women who reach the throne yet abandon modesty, who invoke Heaven while plotting harm, who turn proper dress upside down on the bed, and whose passions shift with every phase of the moon—
value.literal: As for those paired to the apex yet deficient in restraint, who rely on heaven to work calamity, who overturn upper and lower garments upon the mat, and feel lust askew at first quarter and full moon.

value.zh: 則龍漦結釁，宗周鞠為黍苗；
value.en: —dragon spit seals a fatal feud, and the Zhou heartland turns to weed-grown ruin;
value.literal: Then dragon-spittle knots disaster, and royal Zhou becomes nothing but millet shoots;

value.zh: 燕尾挻災，隆漢墜其枌社矣。
value.en: swallow-tail charms invite catastrophe, and even mighty Han loses its soil-and-millet shrines.
value.literal: Swallow tails draw calamity, and flourishing Han drops its mulberry altars.

value.zh: 自曹劉內主，位以色登，甄衛之家，榮非德舉。
value.en: Under the Cao and Liu courts, palace ladies rose by looks alone; clans such as the Zhens and Weis won favor without moral merit.
value.literal: Since the inner mistresses of Cao and Liu, position climbed by beauty; in the households of Zhen and Wei, glory was not raised by virtue.

value.zh: 淫荒挺性，蔑西郊之禮容；
value.en: Wanton temperaments mocked the solemn suburban liturgy reserved for the empress;
value.literal: Dissolute and wasteful by nature, they slighted the ritual bearing of the western suburb;

value.zh: 婉孌含辭，作南國之奇態。
value.en: Soft voices and studied phrases invented the freakish grace of southern entertainers.
value.literal: Soft loveliness holding coy phrases, they fashioned exotic manners of the southern states.

value.zh: 詖謁由斯外人，穢德於是內宣。
value.en: Sycophancy leaked beyond the palace gates while depravity was preached inside.
value.literal: Slanderous flattery thereby passed outward, and foul conduct was proclaimed within.

value.zh: 椒掖播晨牝之風，蘭殿絕河雎之響。
value.en: The harem aired the omen of women ruling like crowing hens; orchid halls no longer echoed the chaste songs of “Guan ju.”
value.literal: The pepper chambers spread the wind of the hen crowing at dawn; the orchid halls cut off the echo of “Guan ju” by the River.

value.zh: 永言彤史，大練之範逾微；
value.en: Forever the palace diarists wrote, yet the ideal of homespun austerity faded;
value.literal: Speaking long of the vermilion scribe, the model of coarse white silk grows ever fainter;

value.zh: 緬視青蒲，脫珥之猷替矣。
value.en: Looking back to mat audiences where consorts remonstrated, the counsel of tearing off earrings to warn the throne had vanished.
value.literal: Gazing afar at the green rushes, the strategy of casting off ear-jewels is replaced.

value.zh: 晉承其末，與世污隆，宣皇創基，功弘而道屈；
value.en: The Jin took up this fallen era and rose or fell with the times. Emperor Xuan laid the foundations: his deeds were grand, yet the moral course stayed cramped;
value.literal: Jin inherited the late age; with the world it sank and rose. Emperor Xuan founded the base—achievement broad yet the Way bent;

value.zh: 穆后一善，勣侔於十亂。
value.en: a single virtue in Empress Mu rivaled the merit of the “ten turbulent” worthies who saved a dynasty.
value.literal: one goodness of Empress Mu—merit equal to the Ten Disorderly Ones.

value.zh: 洎乎世祖，[1]始親選良家，既而帝掩紈扇，躬行請託。
value.en: Under Emperor Wu [1] the court at first picked brides from respectable houses; soon the sovereign waved his silk fan in the inner quarters and himself traded favors for appointments.
value.literal: Down to Shizu [1], he began personally selecting from good families; thereafter the emperor hid behind the silk fan and personally practiced solicitation.

value.zh: 后採長白，實彰妒忌之情；
value.en: An empress chosen for graying hair laid bare the spite of jealousy;
value.literal: The empress chose “long white,” truly displaying jealousy;

value.zh: 賈納短青，竟踐覆亡之轍。
value.en: the Jias welcomed a young rival and eventually followed the same rut to ruin.
value.literal: Jia took in “short green,” and in the end trod the rut of overthrow.

value.zh: 得失遺跡，煥在綈緗，興滅所由，義同畫一。
value.en: Success and failure still gleam from the silk-bound histories; the springs of fortune and disaster follow one clear pattern.
value.literal: Tracks of gain and loss shine forth on silk documents; the causes of rise and ruin share one uniform pattern in meaning.

value.zh: 故列其本事，以為后妃傳云。
value.en: I therefore set out the essential facts as this “Treatise on Empresses and Consorts.”
value.literal: Therefore I array their basic affairs to form this treatise on empresses and consorts.

value.zh: 駿既死，詔使後軍將軍荀悝送后于永寧宮。
value.en: After Yang Jun fell, Rear-General Xun Kui was ordered to move her to Yongning Palace.
value.literal: After Jun died, an edict ordered Rear-General Xun Kui to escort the empress to Yongning Palace.

value.zh: 特全后母高都君龐氏之命，聽就后居止。
value.en: Her mother Lady Pang was spared and permitted to live with her.
value.literal: Her mother Lady Pang of Gaodu Commandery was specially spared and allowed to stay with the dowager.

value.zh: 賈后諷群公有司奏曰：「皇太后陰漸姦謀，圖危社稷，飛箭繫書，要募將士，同惡相濟，自絕于天。
value.en: Jia’s faction petitioned: “The dowager schemed treason, imperiled the state, shot letters beyond the walls, and recruited troops—criminals helped her and Heaven abandoned her.
value.literal: Empress Jia prompted assembled dukes and offices to memorialize: “The empress dowager secretly carried treason, plotted against the altars, flew arrows with letters tied, summoned soldiers—wicked men aided her and she cut herself off from Heaven.

value.zh: 魯侯絕文姜，春秋所許，蓋以奉順祖宗，任至公於天下。
value.en: Lu cut ties with Wen Jiang, which the Annals condone, to serve ancestors and justice.
value.literal: Duke Lu cut off Wen Jiang—the Spring and Autumn approves—because one must honor ancestors and hold utmost fairness toward the realm.

value.zh: 陛下雖懷無已之情，臣下不敢奉詔。
value.en: We know your grief, sire, yet we cannot sanction mercy.
value.literal: Although Your Majesty harbors endless feeling, your servants dare not obey the edict.

value.zh: 可宣敕王公于朝堂會議。」
value.en: Summon princes and ministers to the outer court for debate.”
value.literal: Let an order proclaim that kings and dukes convene in the court hall to deliberate.”

value.zh: 詔曰：「此大事，更詳之。」
value.en: The throne replied, “Weighty—deliberate further.”
value.literal: An edict said: “This is a great matter—consider it again.”

value.zh: 有司又奏：「駿藉外戚之資，居冢宰之任，陛下既居諒闇，委以重權，至乃陰圖凶逆，布樹私黨。
value.en: They answered: “Yang Jun used kinship to seize power; while you mourned he plotted rebellion and packed offices with clients.
value.literal: The offices again memorialized: “Jun relied on affinal backing and held prime minister’s charge; while Your Majesty mourned in the dark palace he received heavy trust, yet secretly plotted treason and planted private partisans.

value.zh: 皇太后內為脣齒，協同逆謀，禍釁既彰，背捍詔命，阻兵負眾，血刃宮省，而復流書募眾，以獎凶黨，上背祖宗之靈，下絕億兆之望。
value.en: The dowager abetted him; when crime surfaced she resisted orders, armed her faction, and stained the palace—yet still shot appeals to arm traitors, dishonoring spirits and people.
value.literal: The empress dowager was his lip and tooth within; she joined the wicked plot. Once the stench showed, she defied decrees, blocked armies, and bloodied the palace—yet still flew letters to recruit crowds and reward villains, betraying ancestors above and cutting off the myriad hopes below.

value.zh: 昔文姜與亂，春秋所貶，呂宗叛戾，高后降配，宜廢皇太后為峻陽庶人。」
value.en: Like Wen Jiang or Empress Lü, she must be struck from dowager rank and made a commoner of Junyang.”
value.literal: Formerly Wen Jiang joined turmoil—the Spring and Autumn demoted her; the Lü clan rebelled and Empress Gao was lowered in pairing. She should be demoted from empress dowager to commoner of Junyang.”

value.zh: 中書監張華等以為「太后非得罪于先帝者也，今黨惡所親，[3]為不母于聖世。
value.en: Zhang Hua argued: “She never wronged Emperor Wu; siding with villains now breaks maternal duty in our era [3].
value.literal: Palace Supervisor Zhang Hua and others held: “The dowager did not offend the late emperor; now she joins wicked kin—she fails motherhood toward this sage age [3].

value.zh: 宜依孝成趙皇后故事，曰武帝皇后，處之離宮，以全貴終之恩。」
value.en: Treat her like Chengdi’s Zhao—call her Emperor Wu’s consort, lodge her apart, yet grant a decent end.”
value.literal: She should follow Empress Zhao of Emperor Cheng’s precedent—styled Empress of Emperor Wu and housed in a detached palace to preserve honored kindness to the end.”

value.zh: 尚書令、下邳王晃等議曰：「皇太后與駿潛謀，欲危社稷，不可復奉承宗廟，配合先帝。
value.en: Wang Huang countered: “She conspired with Yang Jun—she cannot share Wu’s temple.
value.literal: Minister Director Prince Kang of Xiapi Huan and others debated: “The empress dowager secretly plotted with Jun to overturn the state—she cannot again serve the temple or pair with the late emperor.

value.zh: 宜貶尊號，廢詣金墉城。」
value.en: Strip her titles and lock her in Jinyong.”
value.literal: Her honored title should be stripped and she banished to Metal-Walled Fortress.”

value.zh: 于是有司奏：「請從晃等議，廢太后為庶人。
value.en: Officials petitioned: "We ask to adopt Huang's proposal and depose the dowager as a commoner.
value.literal: Thereupon the offices petitioned: “We ask following Huang’s proposal—depose the dowager as commoner.

value.zh: 遣使者以太牢告于郊廟，以奉承祖宗之命，稱萬國之望。
value.en: Announce it with suburban bull sacrifice to ancestors and satisfy the realm.
value.literal: Dispatch envoys with grand sacrifice to announce at suburban altars and ancestral temple, obeying ancestor spirits and answering myriad lands’ expectation.

value.zh: 至於諸所供奉，可順聖恩，務從豐厚。」
value.en: Let her maintenance stay generous per your mercy.”
value.literal: As for all provisions supplied, follow sagely kindness and strive for abundance.”

value.zh: 詔不許。
value.en: The emperor refused.
value.literal: The edict did not permit.

value.zh: 有司又固請，乃可之。
value.en: They insisted again; he yielded.
value.literal: The offices pressed again; then he consented.

value.zh: 又奏：「楊駿造亂，家屬應誅，詔原其妻龐命，以慰太后之心。
value.en: They added: “Yang Jun’s clan should die; you spared Lady Pang to comfort the dowager.
value.literal: They also memorialized: “Yang Jun raised rebellion—his kin deserve execution; the edict spared his wife Pang to console the dowager.

value.zh: 今太后廢為庶人，請以龐付廷尉行刑。」
value.en: Now that she is a commoner, execute Lady Pang.”
value.literal: Now that the dowager is demoted to commoner, we ask that Pang be handed to the Commandant of Justice for execution.”

value.zh: 詔曰：「聽龐與庶人相隨。」
value.en: He ruled: “Let Lady Pang stay with her.”
value.literal: The edict said: “Let Pang follow the commoner.”

value.zh: 有司希賈后旨，固請，乃從之。
value.en: Bowing to Jia’s will they insisted until he agreed.
value.literal: The offices, courting Empress Jia’s intent, pressed firmly; then he followed.

value.zh: 龐臨刑，太后抱持號叫，截髮稽顙，上表詣賈后稱妾，請全母命，不見省。
value.en: At Lady Pang’s execution the dowager clung to her, cut her hair, kowtowed, signed herself Jia’s servant to beg for mercy—Jia ignored her.
value.literal: When Pang faced execution, the empress dowager clutched her, wailing; she cut her hair and knocked her forehead, submitted a memorial as concubine to Empress Jia begging to save her mother’s life—she was not granted audience.

value.zh: 初，太后尚有侍御十餘人，賈后奪之，絕膳而崩，時年三十四，在位十五年。
value.en: Jia stripped her servants; she starved at thirty-four after fifteen years as consort.
value.literal: At first the dowager still had more than ten attendants; Empress Jia seized them; she starved and died, aged thirty-four, having held rank fifteen years.

value.zh: 賈后又信妖巫，謂太后必訴冤先帝，乃覆而殯之，施諸厭劾符書藥物。
value.en: Jia feared her ghost would accuse Emperor Wu, so she buried her prone under talismans.
value.literal: Empress Jia further trusted witchcraft, fearing the dowager would appeal her grievance to the late emperor; she therefore buried her face-down with curse charms and drugs.

value.zh: 陳騫
value.en: Chen Qian
value.literal: Chen Qian

value.zh: 頠深慮賈后亂政，與司空張華、侍中賈模議廢之而立謝淑妃。
value.en: Fearing Jia Nanfeng's misrule, he plotted with Zhang Hua and Jia Mo to replace her with Lady Xie.
value.literal: Yi deeply feared Empress Jia would disorder the government; together with Minister of Works Zhang Hua and Palace Attendant Jia Mo he discussed deposing her and enthroning Consort Xie.

value.zh: 華、模皆曰：「帝自無廢黜之意，若吾等專行之，上心不以為是。
value.en: "The emperor never meant to depose her," Zhang and Jia replied; acting alone would anger him.
value.literal: Hua and Mo both said: "The emperor himself has no intent to dismiss her; if we act alone in this, in his heart he will not approve.

value.zh: 且諸王方剛，朋黨異議，恐禍如發機，身死國危，無益社稷。」
value.en: The martial princes split into factions; forcing the issue might spring a trap that kills us without saving the realm."
value.literal: Moreover the princes are just now forceful; factions argue differently—we fear disaster would strike like a spring-trigger—our deaths and the state's peril would benefit the altars not at all."

value.zh: 頠曰：「誠如公慮。
value.en: True enough," Yi conceded.
value.literal: Yi said: "Truly it is as you fear.

value.zh: 但昏虐之人，無所忌憚，亂可立待，將如之何？」
value.en: Yet a reckless tyrant invites instant chaos—what then?"
value.literal: Yet a benighted and cruel person fears nothing; chaos can arrive at once—what then are we to do?"

value.zh: 華曰：「卿二人猶且見信，然勤為左右陳禍福之戒，冀無大悖。
value.en: Stay close and lecture him on fortune and ruin," Zhang urged.
value.literal: Hua said: "You two are still trusted; diligently instruct him left and right on the consequences of fortune and disaster, and perhaps there will be no great rebellion.

value.zh: 幸天下尚安，庶可優遊卒歲。」
value.en: While peace lasts we might survive."
value.literal: Fortunately the realm is still calm; perhaps we can drift through our years."

value.zh: 此謀遂寢。
value.en: They dropped the plot.
value.literal: This plan then was abandoned.

value.zh: 頠旦夕勸說從母廣城君，令戒喻賈后親待太子而已。
value.en: Yi besought Aunt Guangcheng daily to teach Nanfeng to honor the heir.
value.literal: Morning and evening Yi urged his maternal aunt the Lady of Guangcheng to instruct Empress Jia to cherish the heir apparent.

value.zh: 或說頠曰：「幸與中宮內外可得盡言。
value.en: Someone advised Wei, "Fortunately, with those inside and outside the central palace, you can speak fully.
value.literal: Someone advised Wei, "Fortunately, with those inside and outside the central palace, you can speak fully.

value.zh: 言若不行，則可辭病摒退。
value.en: If ignored, resign on grounds of illness.
value.literal: If your words do not prevail, you may plead illness and withdraw.

value.zh: 若二者不立，雖有十表，難乎免矣。」
value.en: Otherwise ten memorials will not spare you."
value.literal: If neither course can be established, though you submit ten memorials, escape will be hard."

value.zh: 頠慨然久之，而竟不能行。
value.en: Yi brooded yet never acted.
value.literal: Yi sighed deeply for a long time but in the end could not act.

value.zh: 時以陳准子匡、韓蔚子嵩並侍東宮，頠諫曰：「東宮之建，以儲皇極。
value.en: At the time, Chen Zhun's son Kuang and Han Wei's son Song were both serving in the Eastern Palace. Wei remonstrated, saying, "The Eastern Palace is established to uphold the heir as the imperial pole.
value.literal: At the time, Chen Zhun's son Kuang and Han Wei's son Song were both serving in the Eastern Palace. Wei remonstrated, saying, "The establishment of the Eastern Palace is to store up the imperial standard.

value.zh: 其所與遊接，必簡英俊，宜用成德。
value.en: Its companions must be seasoned worthies.
value.literal: Those who lodge and associate there must be chosen from the talented and heroic; men of completed virtue should serve.

value.zh: 匡、嵩幼弱，未識人理立身之節。
value.en: Kuang and Song were mere boys ignorant of duty.
value.literal: Kuang and Song are young and weak and do not grasp the norms of conduct.

value.zh: 東宮實體夙成之表，而今有童子侍從之聲，未是光闡遐風之弘理也。」
value.en: The Eastern Palace is in substance the sign of early maturity, but now there is the sound of children attending there; this is not the broad principle by which to make distant custom shine forth."
value.literal: The Eastern Palace is in substance the sign of early maturity, but now there is the sound of children attending there; this is not the broad principle by which to make distant custom shine forth."

value.zh: 湣懷太子之廢也，頠與張華苦爭不從，語在《華傳》。
value.en: Yi and Zhang Hua fought bitterly against Minhuai's removal—the fuller story sits in Zhang's biography.
value.literal: When Crown Prince Minhuai was deposed, Yi with Zhang Hua bitterly disputed but was not heeded—the account is in Hua's biography.

value.zh: 初，趙王倫諂事賈后，頠甚惡之，倫數求官，頠與張華復固執不許，由是深為倫所怨。
value.en: Sima Lun curried Jia Nanfeng's favor while Yi and Zhang Hua blocked his offices, planting a deadly grudge.
value.literal: At first the Prince of Zhao, Sima Lun, fawned on Empress Jia; Yi loathed him. Lun repeatedly sought promotion; Yi and Zhang Hua steadfastly refused—thereby earning Lun's bitter hatred.

value.zh: 倫又潛懷篡逆，欲先除朝望，因廢賈后之際遂誅之，時年三十四。
value.en: Lun used Jia's fall as cover to murder Yi at thirty-four while plotting a coup.
value.literal: Lun also nursed usurpation: wishing first to eliminate eminent ministers, he executed Yi while deposing the empress; Yi was thirty-four.

value.zh: 二子嵩、該，倫亦欲害之。
value.en: Lun targeted Yi's sons Song and Gai next.
value.literal: His sons Song and Gai—Lun meant to kill them too.

value.zh: 梁王肜、東海王越稱頠父秀有勳王室，配食太廟，不宜滅其後嗣，故得不死，徙帶方；
value.en: Princes Sima Rong of Liang and Sima Yue of Donghai declared that Yi's father Xiu had served the dynasty and received offerings in the Grand Temple—his line must not be extinguished—so the boys lived on, banished to Daifang.
value.literal: Princes Sima Rong of Liang and Sima Yue of Donghai declared that Yi's father Xiu had served the dynasty and received offerings in the Grand Temple—his line must not be extinguished—so the boys lived on, banished to Daifang.

value.zh: 惠帝反正，追復頠本官，改葬以卿禮，諡曰成。
value.en: After Hui's restoration Yi won reinstatement, a proper reburial, and the posthumous name Cheng.
value.literal: When Emperor Hui was restored, Yi's offices were posthumously reinstated; he was reburied with ministerial ceremony and titled Cheng.

value.zh: 以嵩嗣爵，為中書黃門侍郎。
value.en: The marquisate passed to Song in the central secretariat.
value.literal: Song inherited the title and became palace attendant and palace secretary.

value.zh: 該出後從伯凱，為散騎常侍，並為乞活賊陳午所害。
value.en: Gai had been adopted out to his father's cousin Kai; he was supernumerary attendant until both brothers fell to Chen Wu's Qi Huo band.
value.literal: Gai had been adopted out to his father's cousin Kai; he was supernumerary attendant until both brothers fell to Chen Wu's Qi Huo band.

value.zh: 楷長子輿先娶亮女，女適衛瓘子，楷慮內難未已，求出外鎮，除安南將軍、假節、都督荊州諸軍事，垂當發而瑋果矯詔誅亮、瓘。
value.en: Marriage ties to both factions drove Kai toward Jingzhou—Wei's forged orders struck first.
value.literal: Kai's heir Yu had first married Sima Liang's daughter, and Kai's daughter was married to a son of Wei Guan—fearing civil war Kai sought a province; made General Who Pacifies the South, with staff, commanding Jingzhou military affairs—just as he prepared to march, Wei forged an edict killing Liang and Guan.

value.zh: 瑋以楷前奪己中候，又與亮、瓘婚親，密遣討楷。
value.en: Wei sent killers after Kai for family links to his victims.
value.literal: Wei because Kai had earlier displaced him from Central Commander and was also marriage kin to Liang and Guan secretly sent forces against Kai.

value.zh: 楷素知瑋有望于己，聞有變，單車入城，匿于妻父王渾家，與亮小子一夜八徙，故得免難。
value.en: He dodged patrols by hiding with Wang Hun and Liang's orphan.
value.literal: Kai had always known Wei bore him ill will; hearing of the upheaval, he drove alone into the city and hid in his father-in-law Wang Hun's house; with Liang's youngest son he moved eight times in one night—thus he escaped harm.

value.zh: 瑋既伏誅，以楷為中書令，加侍中，與張華、王戎並管機要。
value.en: Wei fell and Kai joined Zhang Hua and Wang Rong at power's core.
value.literal: After Wei died Kai directed the palace secretariat with Zhang Hua and Wang Rong.

value.zh: 楷有渴利疾，不樂處勢。
value.en: Diabetes-like thirst made central office unbearable.
value.literal: Kai suffered wasting thirst and loathed heavy responsibility.

value.zh: 王渾為楷請曰：「楷受先帝拔擢之恩，復蒙陛下寵遇，誠竭節之秋也。
value.en: Wang Hun made a request on Kai's behalf, saying, "Kai received the grace of being promoted by the former emperor and again has received Your Majesty's favor and treatment; truly this is the autumn for exhausting his integrity.
value.literal: Wang Hun made a request on Kai's behalf, saying, "Kai received the grace of being promoted by the former emperor and again has received Your Majesty's favor and treatment; truly this is the autumn for exhausting his integrity.

value.zh: 然楷性不競於物，昔為常侍，求出為河內太守；
value.en: Yet Kai's nature does not compete with things. Formerly, when he was Regular Attendant, he sought to go out as Grand Administrator of Henei.
value.literal: Yet Kai's nature does not compete with things. Formerly, when he was Regular Attendant, he sought to go out as Grand Administrator of Henei.

value.zh: 後為侍中，復求出為河南尹；
value.en: Later, when he was Palace Attendant, he again sought to go out as Governor of Henan.
value.literal: Later, when he was Palace Attendant, he again sought to go out as Governor of Henan.

value.zh: 與楊駿不平，求為衛尉；
value.en: When he was not on good terms with Yang Jun, he sought to become Chamberlain for the Palace Garrison.
value.literal: When he was not on good terms with Yang Jun, he sought to become Chamberlain for the Palace Garrison.

value.zh: 及轉東宮，班在時類之下，安於淡退，有識有以見其心也。
value.en: When he was transferred to the Eastern Palace, his rank was below those of his time and class, yet he was at ease in plain withdrawal. Those with understanding had means to see his mind.
value.literal: When he was transferred to the Eastern Palace, his rank was below those of his time and class, yet he was at ease in plain withdrawal. Those with understanding had means to see his mind.

value.zh: 楷今委頓，臣深憂之。
value.en: Kai is now worn down, and I am deeply worried about him.
value.literal: Kai is now worn down, and I am deeply worried about him.

value.zh: 光祿勳缺，以為可用。
value.en: The office of Chamberlain for the Splendid Blessings is vacant, and I think he can be used there.
value.literal: The office of Chamberlain for the Splendid Blessings is vacant, and I think he can be used there.

value.zh: 今張華在中書，王戎在尚書，足舉其契，無為復令楷入，名臣不多，當見將養，不違其志，要其遠濟之益。」
value.en: Now Zhang Hua is in the Palace Secretariat, and Wang Rong is in the Department of State Affairs; they are enough to raise what fits. There is no need to make Kai enter again. Eminent ministers are not many, and he should be cared for and nourished, without violating his will, so as to seek his long-range benefit."
value.literal: Now Zhang Hua is in the Palace Secretariat, and Wang Rong is in the Department of State Affairs; they are enough to raise what fits. There is no need to make Kai enter again. Eminent ministers are not many, and he should be cared for and nourished, without violating his will, so as to seek his long-range benefit."

value.zh: 不聽，就加光祿大夫、開府儀同三司。
value.en: The throne instead piled on Household Grandee and three-duke parity.
value.literal: [The emperor] did not listen; [Kai] was additionally given Household Grandee and allowed to maintain a separate headquarters with ceremony equal to the Three Dukes.

value.zh: 及疾篤，詔遣黃門郎王衍省疾，楷回眸矚之曰：「竟未相識。」
value.en: When his illness became severe, the edict sent Yellow Gate Gentleman Wang Yan to inspect his illness. Kai turned his eyes back and gazed at him, saying, "In the end, we never came to know one another."
value.literal: When his illness became severe, the edict sent Yellow Gate Gentleman Wang Yan to inspect his illness. Kai turned his eyes back and gazed at him, saying, "In the end, we never came to know one another."

value.zh: 衍深歎其神俊。
value.en: Yan stood awed by that dying brilliance.
value.literal: Yan deeply sighed at his spiritual brilliance.

value.zh: 魏舒，字陽元，任城樊人也。
value.en: Wei Shu, whose courtesy name was Yangyuan, came from Fan in Rencheng commandery.
value.literal: Wei Shu, courtesy name Yangyuan, was a man of Fan in Rencheng.

value.zh: 少孤，為外家寧氏所養。
value.en: He lost his father while still young and was brought up by his mother's people, the Nings.
value.literal: In youth he was orphaned and was reared by his maternal kin, the Ning clan.

value.zh: 寧氏起宅，相宅者云：「當出貴甥。」
value.en: When the Nings raised a new house, a geomancer told them, "This site will produce a distinguished nephew."
value.literal: The Ning family built a house, and a geomancer of the site said, "A noble nephew will come forth."

value.zh: 外祖母以魏氏甥小而慧，意謂應之。
value.en: His maternal grandmother, seeing that the Wei boy was young but bright, assumed the omen pointed to him.
value.literal: His maternal grandmother, because the Wei nephew was small yet clever, in her mind thought it referred to him.

value.zh: 舒曰：「當為外氏成此宅相。」
value.en: Shu said, "It falls to me to fulfill that houselot prophecy for our mother's family."
value.literal: Shu said, "I shall for the maternal clan complete this houselot omen."

value.zh: 久乃別居。
value.en: Only after many years did he move out and keep a separate household.
value.literal: After a long time then he lived apart.

value.zh: 身長八尺二寸，姿望秀偉，飲酒石餘，而遲鈍質樸，不為鄉親所重。
value.en: He stood eight chi and two cun tall, carried himself with striking presence, and could put away more than a shi of wine, yet he seemed slow and unpolished, so neighbors and relatives thought little of him.
value.literal: His body was eight chi two cun in height, his bearing fine and grand, he drank more than a shi of wine, yet was slow, dull, plain, and was not esteemed by townsmen and kin.

value.zh: 從叔父吏部郎衡，有名當世，亦不之知，使守水碓，每歎曰：「舒堪數百戶長，我願畢矣！」
value.en: His paternal uncle Heng, a Personnel Ministry officer celebrated in their day, never recognized his gifts either and set him to mind the water-powered mill, sighing, "If Shu can serve as headman over a few hundred households, I shall ask nothing more!"
value.literal: His father's cousin Heng, Personnel Ministry gentleman, had fame in the age, also did not know him, made him guard the water trip-hammer, and often sighed, saying, "Shu can suffice as chief of several hundred households — my wishes are fulfilled!"

value.zh: 舒亦不以介意。
value.en: Shu did not resent him for it.
value.literal: Shu also did not on that account take it to mind.

value.zh: 不修常人之節，不為皎曆之事，每欲容才長物，終不顯人之短。
value.en: He scorned petty convention and avoided ostentatious moralism, preferring always to nurture others' strengths and never to expose their faults.
value.literal: He did not cultivate ordinary men's scruples, did not do bright-harsh matters, always wished to accommodate talent and lengthen things, and to the end did not display people's shortcomings.

value.zh: 性好騎射，著韋衣。
value.en: He loved riding and archery and habitually dressed in leather hunting clothes.
value.literal: By nature he loved riding and shooting, and wore leather garments.

value.zh: 入山澤，以漁獵為事。
value.en: He roamed hills and wetlands and made fishing and hunting his chief pastime.
value.literal: He entered mountains and marshes and took fishing and hunting as his occupation.

value.zh: 唯太原王乂謂舒曰：「卿終當為台輔，然今未能令妻子免饑寒，吾當助卿營之。」
value.en: Wang Yi of Taiyuan alone told him, "You are destined for the highest councils of state, yet you cannot yet keep your wife and children from want; let me help you set them up."
value.literal: Only Wang Yi of Taiyuan said to Shu, "You in the end will become a pillar minister, yet now are not able to cause wife and children to escape cold and hunger; I shall help you arrange it."

value.zh: 常振其匱乏，舒受而不辭。
value.en: Wang regularly supplied what the household lacked, and Shu accepted without demur.
value.literal: He regularly relieved their want; Shu accepted and did not decline.

value.zh: 舒嘗詣野王，主人妻夜產，俄而聞車馬之聲，相問曰：「男也，女也？」
value.en: On a visit to Yewang, while his host's wife labored in the night, voices like chariots and horses suddenly sounded outside, asking, "Boy or girl?"
value.literal: Shu once went to Yewang; the host's wife gave birth in the night; presently they heard the sound of horses and chariots, mutually asking, "Male or female?"

value.zh: 曰：「男，書之，十五以兵死。」
value.en: The answer came: "A son. Record it—he will die by the sword at fifteen."
value.literal: It was said, "Male; write it; at fifteen he will die by weapons."

value.zh: 復問：「寢者為誰？」
value.en: Then they asked, "Who lies abed here?"
value.literal: Again they asked, "Who is the one sleeping?"

value.zh: 曰：「魏公舒。」
value.en: The reply was, "Lord Wei Shu."
value.literal: It was said, "Lord Wei Shu."

value.zh: 後十五載，詣主人，問所生兒何在，曰：「因條桑為斧傷而死。」
value.en: Fifteen years later he looked up the host and asked after that child; the man said, "He died when an axe slipped as he was pruning mulberry."
value.literal: After fifteen years he went to the host, asked where the born child was, and it was said, "Because trimming mulberry he was wounded by an axe and died."

value.zh: 舒自知當為公矣。
value.en: Shu understood then that he was fated to rise to the rank of duke.
value.literal: Shu himself knew he would become a duke.

value.zh: 太康初，拜右僕射。
value.en: Early in the Taikang era he was appointed right vice-director of the Masters of Writing.
value.literal: At the beginning of Taikang he was appointed Right Supervisor of the Masters of Writing.

value.zh: 舒與衛瓘、山濤、張華等以六合混一，宜用古典封禪東嶽，前後累陳其事，帝謙讓不許。
value.en: Shu joined Wei Guan, Shan Tao, Zhang Hua, and others in arguing that, with the realm reunited, the court ought to revive the classical Feng and Shan sacrifices on Mount Tai; they pressed the point in memorial after memorial, but the emperor modestly refused.
value.literal: Shu together with Wei Guan, Shan Tao, Zhang Hua, and others, because the six directions were mixed in one, held it proper to use classical rites to feng and shan at the eastern marchmount; before and after repeatedly they presented this matter; the emperor modestly yielded and did not permit.

value.zh: 以舒為左僕射，領吏部。
value.en: Shu was named left vice-director of the Masters of Writing and placed in charge of the Personnel Ministry.
value.literal: They appointed Shu Left Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, concurrently heading the Personnel Ministry.

value.zh: 舒上言：「今選六宮，聘以玉帛，而舊使禦府丞奉聘，宣成嘉禮，贄重使輕。
value.en: Shu memorialized: "Selection for the six palaces still relies on jade and silk betrothal gifts, yet we continue to send the deputy superintendent of the palace storehouse as envoy—the treasure is weighty while the messenger is slight.
value.literal: Shu submitted words: "Now in selecting the six palaces betrothal uses jade and silk, yet the old practice sends the Palace Storehouse deputy to carry betrothal, proclaiming and completing the fine rite, while the gifts are heavy and the envoy light.

value.zh: 以為拜三夫人宜使卿，九嬪使五官中郎將，美人、良人使謁者，於典制為弘。」
value.en: I propose that investiture of the three senior consorts be entrusted to ministers, the nine imperial concubines to gentlemen of the household for all purposes, and the lower ranks of palace ladies to court heralds—so the ritual weight matches the statutes."
value.literal: I hold that for investing the three great consorts it is proper to use ministers, for the nine concubines to use Gentlemen of the Household for All Purposes, for beauties and chosen ladies to use heralds — toward canonical regulation this is magnified."

value.zh: 有詔詳之，眾議異同，遂寢。
value.en: The court ordered a full discussion, but opinions clashed and the plan was shelved.
value.literal: There was an edict to deliberate it in detail; the crowd's discussions differed in agreement, and therefore it slept.

value.zh: 加右光祿大夫、儀同三司。
value.en: He received the additional titles of grand master of the right and privilege equal to the Three Dukes.
value.literal: He was added Grand Master of the Right with parity of the Three Dukes.

value.zh: 劉毅
value.en: Liu Yi.
value.literal: Liu Yi.

value.zh: 吳平，以參謀議功，賜弟郁爵汝南亭侯。
value.en: After Wu was pacified, for He Jiao’s merit in planning counsel his younger brother Yu was granted the rank of Marquis of Runan Pavilion.
value.literal: When Wu was pacified—for planning merit—granted younger brother Yu noble rank Marquis of Runan Pavilion.

value.zh: 嶠轉侍中，愈被親禮，與任愷、張華相善。
value.en: As palace attendant he grew closer to the throne and befriended Ren Kai and Zhang Hua.
value.literal: Jiao transferred to palace attendant—more favored—in friendship with Ren Kai and Zhang Hua.

value.zh: 嶠見太子不令，因侍坐曰：「皇太子有淳古之風，而季世多偽，恐不了陛下家事。」
value.en: At leisure he said: "The crown prince has an antique plainness, yet a decadent age breeds sham—I fear he cannot manage Your Majesty's household."
value.literal: Jiao seeing heir apparent was not sound—therefore sitting attendance said: "Crown prince has pure antique manner—but declining age abounds in sham—fears he cannot manage Your Majesty’s household affairs."

value.zh: 帝默然不答。
value.en: The emperor stayed silent.
value.literal: Emperor silent—did not answer.

value.zh: 後與荀顗、荀勖同侍，帝曰：「太子近入朝，差長進，卿可俱詣之，粗及世事。」
value.en: Later, with the Xuns attending, the emperor said: "The heir has lately entered court and made some progress—you may all visit him and touch on affairs of state."
value.literal: Later together attending with Xun Yi and Xun Xu—Emperor said: "Heir apparent lately entered court—somewhat grown—you may all visit him—roughly touch on worldly affairs."

value.zh: 即奉詔而還。
value.en: They bowed and withdrew.
value.literal: Immediately obeyed edict and returned.

value.zh: 顗、勖並稱太子明識弘雅，誠如明詔。
value.en: Xun Yi and Xun Xu flattered the prince’s polish.
value.literal: Yi and Xu together praised heir apparent’s bright understanding—vast and refined—truly as enlightened edict.

value.zh: 嶠曰：「聖質如初耳！」
value.en: He Jiao said: "His sagely substance is just as before!"
value.literal: Jiao said: "Sagely substance like first!"

value.zh: 帝不悅而起。
value.en: The emperor rose in anger.
value.literal: Emperor displeased—rose.

value.zh: 嶠退居，恆懷慨歎，知不見用，猶不能已。
value.en: He brooded—knowing his counsel spurned yet unable to stay mute.
value.literal: Jiao withdrew—always harbored sighing regret—knew not employed—still could not stop.

value.zh: 在御坐言及社稷，未嘗不以儲君為憂。
value.en: Whenever talk touched the realm’s fate he fretted over the heir.
value.literal: On imperial seat speaking of altars of soil and grain—never without taking heir as worry.

value.zh: 帝知其言忠，每不酬和。
value.en: The emperor knew him faithful yet refused to engage.
value.literal: Emperor knew his words loyal—each time did not respond in harmony.

value.zh: 後與嶠語，不及來事。
value.en: Later audiences skirted the succession entirely.
value.literal: Later speaking with Jiao—did not reach future matters.

value.zh: 或以告賈妃，妃銜之。
value.en: Word reached Empress Jia—she nursed a grudge.
value.literal: Someone informed Consort Jia—consort bore grudge.

value.zh: 太康末，為尚書，以母憂去職。
value.en: Late in Taikang he headed the ministry until mourning his mother.
value.literal: Late Taikang—became minister of state affairs—left office for mother’s mourning.

value.zh: 愷有經國之幹，萬機大小多管綜之。
value.en: He mastered statecraft large and small.
value.literal: Kai had capacity for ordering the state—myriad threads small and large mostly managed comprehensively.

value.zh: 性忠正，以社稷為己任，帝器而昵之，政事多諮焉。
value.en: Loyal and upright, he took the altars of the state as his own charge; the emperor prized and favored him and consulted him on most government affairs.
value.literal: Nature loyal upright—took altars of soil and grain as self-task—Emperor prized and favored—state affairs mostly consulted.

value.zh: 泰始初，鄭沖、王祥、何曾、荀顗、裴秀等各以老疾歸第。
value.en: Early Taishi the elder ministers retired ill.
value.literal: Taishi beginning—Zheng Chong—Wang Xiang—He Zeng—Xun Yi—Pei Xiu each by old age illness returned mansion.

value.zh: 帝優寵大臣，不欲勞以筋力，數遣愷諭旨于諸公，諮以當世大政，參議得失。
value.en: Wu sent Ren Kai to relay policy to the retired elders.
value.literal: Emperor graciously favored great ministers—did not wish labor them with sinews—often sent Kai conveying intent to each lord—consulting on age’s great policies—debating gain and loss.

value.zh: 愷惡賈充之為人也，不欲令久執朝政，每裁抑焉。
value.en: He worked to curb Jia Chong’s power.
value.literal: Kai hated Jia Chong’s person—did not wish him long hold court governance—each time restrained.

value.zh: 充病之，不知所為。
value.en: Jia Chong despaired.
value.literal: Chong sick at heart—knew not what to do.

value.zh: 後承間言愷忠貞局正，宜在東宮，使護太子。
value.en: He urged posting Ren Kai to tutor the heir—ostensibly praise.
value.literal: Later seizing interval spoke Kai loyal steadfast upright—ought be eastern palace—make protect heir.

value.zh: 帝從之，以為太子少傅，而侍中如故，充計畫不行。
value.en: The emperor followed and made him junior tutor to the heir, remaining palace attendant as before; Chong’s plan did not succeed.
value.literal: Emperor followed—thought junior tutor to heir—palace attendant as before—Chong’s plan did not proceed.

value.zh: 會秦、雍寇擾，天子以為憂。
value.en: Qinzhou and Yongzhou revolted—Wu fretted.
value.literal: When Qin and Yong raided and disturbed—Son of Heaven took as worry.

value.zh: 愷因曰：「秦、涼覆敗，關右騷動，此誠國家之所深慮。
value.en: Ren Kai said: "Qin and Liang have collapsed and the west is in turmoil—this truly is the state's deep worry.
value.literal: Kai therefore said: "Qin and Liang overturned defeated—right of Pass disturbed—this truly state’s deep worry.

value.zh: 宜速鎮撫，使人心有庇。
value.en: It needed a credible marshal to reassure the west.
value.literal: Ought quickly pacify soothe—make people’s hearts have shelter.

value.zh: 自非威望重臣有計略者，無以康西土也。」
value.en: Only a veteran minister of prestige and stratagem can pacify the western lands."
value.literal: Unless prestige-weighted minister with stratagem—none can heal western lands."

value.zh: 帝曰：「誰可任者？」
value.en: “Who fits?” asked the emperor.
value.literal: Emperor said: "Who can be appointed?"

value.zh: 愷曰：「賈充其人也。」
value.en: “Jia Chong,” said Ren Kai—setting a trap.
value.literal: Kai said: "Jia Chong is the man."

value.zh: 中書令庾純亦言之，於是詔充西鎮長安。
value.en: Yu Chun echoed the call—so Jia Chong was ordered west.
value.literal: Director of the palace secretariat Yu Chun also spoke—thereupon edict Chong west guard Chang’an.

value.zh: 充用荀勖計得留。
value.en: Jia Chong used Xun Xu’s ruse to remain at court.
value.literal: Chong using Xun Xu’s plan obtained stay.

value.zh: 充既為帝所遇，欲專名勢，而庾純、張華、溫顒、向秀、和嶠之徒皆與愷善，楊珧、王恂、華廙等充所親敬，於是朋黨紛然。
value.en: Favored by the emperor, Jia Chong wished to monopolize fame and power, while Yu Chun, Zhang Hua, Wen Yong, Xiang Xiu, He Jiao and their like all befriended Kai, and Yang Yao, Wang Xun, and Hua Yi were those Chong held dear, so factional cliques flared.
value.literal: Chong having been favored by Emperor wished monopolize fame and power—while Yu Chun, Zhang Hua, Wen Yong, Xiang Xiu, He Jiao and their like all befriended Kai—Yang Yao, Wang Xun, Hua Yi and such Chong held dear—thereby faction cliques flared.

value.zh: 帝知之，召充、愷宴於式乾殿，而謂充等曰：「朝廷宜一，大臣當和。」
value.en: The emperor summoned both factions to Shiqian Hall and said: "The court should be one; great ministers should harmonize."
value.literal: Emperor knowing it—summoned Chong and Kai to feast at Shiqian Hall—and said to Chong and others: "Court ought be one—great ministers ought harmonize."

value.zh: 充、愷各拜謝而罷。
value.en: Both sides bowed off and left.
value.literal: Chong and Kai each bowed thanks and ceased.

value.zh: 既而充、愷等以帝已知之而不責，結怨愈深，外相崇重，內甚不平。
value.en: Assured the throne would not punish them, Jia Chong and Ren Kai feigned respect while hating each other more.
value.literal: Thereafter Chong, Kai and others because Emperor already knew yet did not blame—knot of hatred grew deeper—outwardly mutual esteem—innerly very unbalanced.

value.zh: 或為充謀曰：「愷總門下樞要，得與上親接，宜啟令典選，便得漸疏，此一都令史事耳。
value.en: A counselor urged Jia Chong: "Ren Kai controls the privy chancery and has intimate access—memorialize to put him in charge of selection and he will grow distant; that is only a capital clerk's affair.
value.literal: Someone for Chong schemed: "Kai governs privy-chamber pivot—gains close access to superiors—ought memorialize to make him superintend selection—then can gradually grow distant—this is one capital clerk’s affair.

value.zh: 且九流難精，間隙易乘。」
value.en: Moreover the nine grades are hard to master—cracks invite attack."
value.literal: Moreover nine currents hard to master—cracks easy to exploit."

value.zh: 充因稱愷才能，宜在官人之職。
value.en: Jia Chong praised Ren Kai’s fitness for personnel.
value.literal: Chong therefore praised Kai’s talent—ought hold office of ordering men.

value.zh: 帝不之疑，謂充舉得其才。
value.en: Emperor Wu trusted the nomination.
value.literal: Emperor did not suspect—said Chong’s recommendation obtained right talent.

value.zh: 即日以愷為吏部尚書，加奉車都尉。
value.en: Ren Kai became minister of personnel with added military rank.
value.literal: Same day appointed Kai minister of personnel—added commandant of palace carriage.

value.zh: 何攀，字惠興，蜀郡郫人也。
value.en: He Pan, styled Huixing, came from Pi in Shu.
value.literal: He Pan, courtesy name Huixing, native of Pi in Shu commandery.

value.zh: 仕州為主薄。
value.en: He began as a provincial chief clerk.
value.literal: Served province as chief clerk.

value.zh: 屬刺史皇甫晏為牙門張弘所害，誣以大逆。
value.en: Inspector Huangfu Yan was murdered by Zhang Hong and smeared as a traitor.
value.literal: When Inspector Huangfu Yan was harmed by camp gate Zhang Hong—slandered with great treason.

value.zh: 時攀適丁母喪，遂詣梁州拜表，證晏不反，故晏冤理得申。
value.en: Though mourning his mother, he rode to Liangzhou and cleared Huangfu Yan’s name.
value.literal: At time Pan happened mourning mother—thereupon went to Liangzhou submitting memorial—proved Yan did not rebel—therefore Yan’s wrong managed to clear.

value.zh: 王濬為益州，辟為別駕。
value.en: Wang Jun made him provincial aide in Yi.
value.literal: Wang Jun as Yi province—summoned as aide.

value.zh: 濬謀伐吳，遣攀奉表詣台，口陳事機，詔再引見，乃令張華與攀籌量進時討之宜。
value.en: He Pan carried Wang Jun’s Wu campaign memorial to Luoyang and planned timing with Zhang Hua.
value.literal: Jun schemed attacking Wu—sent Pan bearing memorial to court—orally stated opportunity—edict twice summoned audience—ordered Zhang Hua with Pan deliberate advancing timing of attack fitness.

value.zh: 濬兼遣攀過羊祜，面陳伐吳之策。
value.en: He also briefed Yang Hu in person on the Wu invasion.
value.literal: Jun also sent Pan visit Yang Hu—face to face state attacking Wu strategies.

value.zh: 攀善於將命，帝善之，詔攀參濬軍事。
value.en: His diplomacy pleased Emperor Wu, who attached him to Wang Jun’s staff.
value.literal: Pan good at carrying orders—Emperor praised—ordered Pan assist Jun military affairs.

value.zh: 及孫皓降于濬，而王渾恚於後機，欲攻濬，攀勸濬送皓與渾，由是事解。
value.en: When Wang Hun nearly attacked Wang Jun over Sun Hao’s surrender, He Pan urged handing the captive to Hun to prevent civil bloodshed.
value.literal: When Sun Hao surrendered to Jun—yet Wang Hun angry at late timing—wished attack Jun—Pan urged Jun deliver Hao to Hun—thereby matter resolved.

value.zh: 以攀為濬輔國司馬，封關內侯。
value.en: Wang Jun named him auxiliary marshal—Marquis Within the Pass.
value.literal: Made Pan Jun aids-state marshal—enfeoffed marquis within Guan.

value.zh: 轉滎陽令，上便宜十事，甚得名稱。
value.en: As Xingyang magistrate he offered ten reform memos and won fame.
value.literal: Transferred Xingyang magistrate—submitted convenient matters ten items—greatly earned reputation.

value.zh: 除廷尉平。
value.en: He became a justice assessor.
value.literal: Appointed commandant-ping of justice.

value.zh: 時廷尉卿諸葛沖以攀蜀士，輕之，及共斷疑獄，沖始嘆服。
value.en: Zhuge Chong sneered at his Shu origins until joint trials proved his genius.
value.literal: At time commandant of justice Zhuge Chong because Pan Shu gentleman—slighted him—when together judged doubtful lawsuits—Chong then sighed admiration.

value.zh: 遷宣城太守，不行，轉散騎侍郎。
value.en: He declined Xuancheng but joined the attendant corps.
value.literal: Promoted prefect of Xuancheng—did not go—transferred regular attendant at casual riding.

value.zh: 楊駿執政，多樹親屬，大開封嘗，欲以恩澤自衛。
value.en: Regent Yang Jun stuffed offices with kin and blanketed them with patents.
value.literal: Yang Jun holding power—planted many kin—greatly opened investitures rewards—wished by grace shield self.

value.zh: 攀以為非，乃與石崇共立議奏之。
value.en: He Pan and Shi Chong jointly condemned the policy.
value.literal: Pan thought not right—thereupon with Shi Chong jointly stood memorial submitting.

value.zh: 語在崇傳。
value.en: (See the biography of Shi Chong.)
value.literal: Language is in Chong biography.

value.zh: 帝不納。
value.en: The emperor ignored them.
value.literal: Emperor did not accept.

value.zh: 以豫誅駿功，封西城侯，邑萬戶，賜絹萬匹，弟逢平卿侯，兄子逵關中侯。
value.en: For merit in executing Yang Jun he was enfeoffed Marquis of Xicheng with ten thousand households and ten thousand bolts of silk; his younger brother Feng became Marquis of Pingqing and his elder brother’s son Kui Marquis Within the Pass.
value.literal: By merit participating executing Jun—enfeoffed marquis of Xicheng—ten thousand households—gift silk ten thousand bolts—younger brother Feng Pingqing marquis—elder brother’s son Kui marquis within Guan.

value.zh: 攀固讓所封戶及絹之半，餘所受者分給中外宗親，略不入己。
value.en: He refused half the silk and fiefs—sharing the rest with kin—keeping nothing.
value.literal: Pan firmly declined half of granted households and silk—remainder received distributed inside outside kin—almost none entered self.

value.zh: 遷翊軍校尉，頃之，出為東羌校尉。
value.en: He became aide colonel then Eastern Qiang colonel.
value.literal: Promoted colonel Who Aids Army—shortly—went out colonel of Eastern Qiang.

value.zh: 徵為揚州刺史，在任三年，遷大司農。
value.en: After three years as Yangzhou inspector he headed the ministry of agriculture.
value.literal: Summoned inspector of Yang province—in office three years—promoted minister of agriculture.

value.zh: 轉兗州刺史，加鷹揚將軍，固讓不就。
value.en: He refused Yanzhou despite general’s banners.
value.literal: Transferred inspector of Yanzhou—added general Who Raises Hawk—firmly declined did not take.

value.zh: 太常成粲、左將軍卞粹勸攀蒞職，中詔又加切厲，攀竟稱疾不起。
value.en: Minister of Ceremonies Cheng Can and General of the Left Bian Cui urged him to take the post; an inner edict grew stern, but Pan claimed illness and would not rise.
value.literal: Minister of ceremonies Cheng Can—general left Bian Cui urged Pan take office—inner edict again stern—Pan ultimately claimed illness did not rise.

value.zh: 及趙王倫篡位，遣使召攀，更稱疾篤。
value.en: Prince Lun’s summons met another refusal—grave illness.
value.literal: When Prince Zhao Lun usurped—sent envoy summon Pan—again claimed grave illness.

value.zh: 倫怒，將誅之，攀不得已，扶疾赴召。
value.en: Lun threatened death—He Pan dragged himself to Luoyang.
value.literal: Lun angry—would execute—Pan had no choice—supported illness answered summons.

value.zh: 卒于洛陽，時年五十八。
value.en: He died there at fifty-eight.
value.literal: Died in Luoyang—age fifty-eight.

value.zh: 攀居心平允，蒞官整肅，愛樂人物，敦儒貴才。
value.en: Fair-minded and orderly in office, he honored scholars and talent.
value.literal: Pan dwelling mind fair—holding office stern—loved delighted men—esteemed Confucian prized talent.

value.zh: 為梁、益二州中正，引致遺滯。
value.en: As Liang-Yi rectifier he recalled unjustly blocked men.
value.literal: As grand rectifier for Liang and Yi provinces—drew in stranded men.

value.zh: 巴西陳壽、閻乂、犍為費立皆西州名士，並被鄉閭所謗，清議十餘年。
value.en: Chen Shou and western scholars suffered decade-long village boycotts.
value.literal: Baixi Chen Shou—Yan Yi—Fei Li of Qianwei—all western province famed gentlemen—together slandered by villages—pure discussion over ten years.

value.zh: 攀申明曲直，咸免冤濫。
value.en: He Pan reversed their verdicts—clearing injustice.
value.literal: Pan clarified crooked straight—all spared wrongful overflow.

value.zh: 攀雖居顯職，家甚貧素，無妾媵伎樂，惟以周窮濟乏為事。
value.en: Despite high rank he stayed poor—no concubines or musicians—only charity.
value.literal: Pan though occupied eminent office—house very poor plain—no concubines singing girls—only took relieving poverty aiding want as task.

value.zh: 子璋嗣，亦有父風。
value.en: Son He Zhang inherited his integrity.
value.literal: Son Zhang succeeded—also had father manner.

value.zh: 愍懷太子
value.en: Crown Prince Minhuai
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 九年六月，有桑生於宮西廂，日長尺餘，數日而枯。
value.en: In the sixth lunar month of the ninth year, a mulberry sprouted in the palace’s west wing. It grew more than a chi each day, then withered after several days.
value.literal: In the sixth lunar month of the ninth year, a mulberry sprouted in the west wing of the palace; it grew more than a chi each day and withered after several days.

value.zh: 十二月，賈后將廢太子，詐稱上不和，呼太子入朝。
value.en: Twelfth month Jia feigned imperial illness to lure Yu to court.
value.literal: In the twelfth month, when Empress Jia would depose the crown prince, she falsely claimed the emperor was unwell and summoned the crown prince to court.

value.zh: 既至，後不見，置於別室，遣婢陳舞賜以酒棗，逼飲醉之。
value.en: She hid him, fed him wine and dates through Chen Wu until he was drunk.
value.literal: When he arrived she did not receive him but lodged him in a side chamber, sent maid Chen Wu with ale and jujubes, and forced him drunk.

value.zh: 使黃門侍郎潘岳作書草，若禱神之文，有如太子素意，因醉而書之，令小婢承福以紙筆及書草使太子書之。
value.en: She had Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Pan Yue draft a prayer text mimicking the Crown Prince's usual intent; because he was drunk she made him copy it, having the young maid Chengfu bring paper, brush, and draft.
value.literal: She had Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Pan Yue draft a prayer text mimicking the crown prince's usual intent; because he was drunk she made him copy it, having the young maid Chengfu bring paper, brush, and draft.

value.zh: 文曰：「陛下宜自了；
value.en: The text read: "Your Majesty should end your own life;
value.literal: The text read: "Your Majesty should end your own life;

value.zh: 不自了，吾當入了之。
value.en: Or I will finish you.
value.literal: if you do not end it yourself, I shall come in and end it for you.

value.zh: 中宮又宜速自了；
value.en: The empress too should quickly end her own life;
value.literal: The empress too should quickly end her own life;

value.zh: 不了，吾當手了之。
value.en: Or I will kill her myself.
value.literal: if she does not, I shall end her life with my own hands.

value.zh: 並謝妃共要克期而兩發，勿疑猶豫，致後患。
value.en: Consort Xie and I strike together—no delay.
value.literal: Together with Consort Xie we agreed a joint date for simultaneous rising—do not hesitate and breed later trouble.

value.zh: 茹毛飲血於三辰之下，皇天許當掃除患害，立道文為王，蔣為內主。
value.en: We shall eat raw flesh and drink blood beneath the three luminaries; High Heaven grants us leave to sweep away the scourge, enthrone Daowen as king, and install Jiang as inner mistress.
value.literal: We shall eat raw flesh and drink blood beneath the three luminaries; High Heaven grants us leave to sweep away the scourge, enthrone Daowen as king, and install Jiang as inner mistress.

value.zh: 願成，當三牲祠北君，大赦天下。
value.en: Then sacrifice to the Northern Lord and amnesty all.
value.literal: When wish is fulfilled we shall sacrifice three victims to the Northern Lord and proclaim an empire-wide amnesty.

value.zh: 要疏如律令。」
value.en: So commands the spell.'
value.literal: Let this sworn petition take effect as commanded.

value.zh: 太子醉迷不覺，遂依而寫之，其字半不成。
value.en: Too drunk and confused to realize what he was doing, the crown prince copied it, but half the characters were incomplete.
value.literal: The crown prince was too drunk and confused to notice; he copied accordingly; half the characters failed to form.

value.zh: 既而補成之，后以呈帝。
value.en: Helpers patched characters before Jia showed Hui.
value.literal: They afterward filled them in; the empress presented it to the emperor.

value.zh: 帝幸式乾殿，召公卿入，使黃門令董猛乙太子書及青紙詔曰：「遹書如此，今賜死。」
value.en: The emperor visited Shi-Qian Hall, summoned dukes and ministers, and had Yellow Gate Chief Dong Meng display the crown prince's script with an edict on blue paper: "Yu has written thus—now sentence him to death."
value.literal: The emperor visited Shi-Qian Hall, summoned dukes and ministers, and had Yellow Gate Chief Dong Meng display the crown prince's script with an edict on blue paper: 'Yu has written thus—now sentence him to death.'

value.zh: 遍示諸公王，莫有言者，惟張華、裴頠證明太子。
value.en: Silence fell until Zhang Hua and Pei Wei defended Yu.
value.literal: No one among lords and dukes spoke except Zhang Hua and Pei Wei who verified the crown prince's innocence.

value.zh: 賈后使董猛矯以長廣公主辭白帝曰：「事宜速決，而群臣各有不同，若有不從詔，宜以軍法從事。」
value.en: Empress Jia had Dong Meng falsely relay Princess Changguang's words to the emperor: "Matters must be settled quickly while ministers disagree—whoever disobeys the edict should face military law."
value.literal: Empress Jia had Dong Meng falsely relay Princess Changguang's words to the emperor: 'Matters must be settled quickly while ministers disagree—whoever disobeys the edict should face military law.'

value.zh: 議至日西不決。
value.en: Debate stalled till dusk.
value.literal: Deliberation lasted until sunset unresolved.

value.zh: 後懼事變，乃表免太子為庶人，詔許之。
value.en: Jia feared delay—demoted Yu to commoner instead.
value.literal: The empress feared events might shift and therefore memorialized to degrade the crown prince to commoner status; an edict approved.

value.zh: 於是使尚書和郁持節，解結為副，及大將軍梁王肜、鎮東將軍淮南王允、前將軍東武公澹、趙王倫、太保何劭詣東宮，廢太子為庶人。
value.en: Thereupon Minister He Yu was dispatched with insignia, with Xie Jie as deputy, together with General-in-Chief Sima Rong, Prince of Liang; Eastern Garrison General Sima Yun, Prince of Huainan; Forward General Sima Dan, Duke of Dongwu; Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao; and Grand Guardian He Shao. They went to the Eastern Palace to depose the crown prince as a commoner.
value.literal: Thereupon Minister He Yu was dispatched with insignia, with Xie Jie as deputy, together with General-in-Chief Sima Rong, Prince of Liang; Eastern Garrison General Sima Yun, Prince of Huainan; Forward General Sima Dan, Duke of Dongwu; Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao; and Grand Guardian He Shao. They went to the Eastern Palace to depose the crown prince as a commoner.

value.zh: 是日太子游玄圃，聞有使者至，改服出崇賢門，再拜受詔，步出承華門，乘粗犢車。
value.en: That day the crown prince roamed the Mystic Garden; hearing envoys arrived he changed clothes, exited Chongxian Gate, twice bowed receiving the edict, walked out Chenghua Gate, and rode a rough ox-cart.
value.literal: That day the crown prince roamed the Mystic Garden; hearing envoys arrived he changed clothes, exited Chongxian Gate, twice bowed receiving the edict, walked out Chenghua Gate, and rode a rough ox-cart.

value.zh: 澹以兵仗送太子妃王氏、三皇孫于金墉城，考竟謝淑妃及太子保林蔣俊。
value.en: Dan escorted Crown Princess Wang and the three imperial grandsons to Jinyong under armed guard, and interrogated Consort Xie and the crown prince’s Lady Baolin Jiang Jun to death.
value.literal: Dan escorted Crown Princess Wang and the three imperial grandsons to Jinyong under armed guard, and interrogated Consort Xie and the crown prince’s Lady Baolin Jiang Jun to death.

value.zh: 明年正月，賈后又使黃門自首，欲與太子為逆。
value.en: Next New Year Jia staged a Yellow Gate confession implicating Yu.
value.literal: The next first month Empress Jia again had a Yellow Gate confess plotting rebellion with the crown prince.

value.zh: 詔以黃門首辭班示公卿。
value.en: An edict circulated the Yellow Gate eunuch’s confession among the dukes and ministers.
value.literal: An edict circulated the confession among dukes and ministers.

value.zh: 又遣澹以千兵防送太子，更幽于許昌宮之別坊，令治書御史劉振持節守之。
value.en: She further sent Dan with a thousand troops to escort the crown prince, moving him to a separate compound of Xuchang palace under Supervising Secretary Liu Zhen with insignia.
value.literal: She further sent Dan with a thousand troops to escort the crown prince, moving him to a separate compound of Xuchang palace under Supervising Secretary Liu Zhen with insignia.

value.zh: 先是，有童謠曰：「東宮馬子莫聾空，前至臘月纏汝閤。」
value.en: Earlier a children's rhyme ran: "Eastern Palace foals—don't plug your ears empty; come twelfth month they'll twine your chamber."
value.literal: Earlier a children's rhyme ran: 'Eastern Palace foals—don't plug your ears empty; come twelfth month they'll twine your chamber.'

value.zh: 又曰：「南風起兮吹白沙，遙望魯國郁嵯峨，千歲髑髏生齒牙。」
value.en: Another went: 'South wind rises blowing white sand; far off Lu kingdom gloomy and tall; thousand-year skulls sprout teeth.'
value.literal: Another went: 'South wind rises blowing white sand; far off Lu kingdom gloomy and tall; thousand-year skulls sprout teeth.'

value.zh: 南風，后名；
value.en: South Wind' meant Empress Jia.
value.literal: South Wind' was the empress's name.

value.zh: 沙門，太子小字也。
value.en: 'Shamen' was the crown prince's childhood byname.
value.literal: 'Shamen' was the crown prince's childhood byname.

value.zh: 時望氣者言廣陵有天子氣，故封為廣陵王，邑五萬戶。
value.en: Astrologers said Guangling bore an emperor's aura, so Yu was made Prince of Guangling with fifty thousand households.
value.literal: At the time, observers of celestial portents said Guangling had the aura of a Son of Heaven; therefore he was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangling with a fief of fifty thousand households.

value.zh: 以劉寔為師，孟珩為友，楊准、馮蓀為文學。
value.en: Liu Shi served as tutor, Meng Heng as companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun as literary aides.
value.literal: Liu Shi was made tutor, Meng Heng companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun literary aides.

value.zh: 惠帝即位，立為皇太子。
value.en: When Hui Di took the throne, Yu was made crown prince.
value.literal: When Emperor Hui succeeded to the throne, he was established as crown prince.

value.zh: 盛選德望以為師傅，以何劭為太師，王戎為太傅，楊濟為太保，裴楷為少師，張華為少傅，和嶠為少保。
value.en: The court recruited eminent tutors—He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.
value.literal: Worthy men of virtue and repute were abundantly selected as tutors and guardians: He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.

value.zh: 元康元年，出就東宮，又詔曰：「遹尚幼蒙，今出東宮，惟當賴師傅群賢之訓。
value.en: In Yuankang year one he moved to the Eastern Palace, and an edict declared: "Yu is still young and inexperienced; now that he has moved to the Eastern Palace he must rely on his tutors and worthy mentors for instruction.
value.literal: In the first year of Yuankang he moved out to the Eastern Palace; an edict further said: "Yu is still young and untutored; now that he is moving out to the Eastern Palace he should rely solely on the instruction of his tutors and the worthy assembly.

value.zh: 其遊處左右，宜得正人使共周旋，能相長益者。」
value.en: Those about him in leisure and attendance should be upright men who keep company with him and help one another improve."
value.literal: Those who attend him in leisure and service should be upright men who may keep company with him and mutually aid one another's growth."

value.zh: 於是使太保衛瓘息庭、司空泰息略、太子太傅楊濟息毖、太子少師裴楷息憲、太子少傅張華息禕、尚書令華暠息恆與太子游處，以相輔導焉。
value.en: Thereupon Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Yang Ji's son Bi, Pei Kai's son Xian, Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Hua Gao's son Heng were sent to keep company with the crown prince and guide him.
value.literal: Thereupon Grand Guardian Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Grand Mentor to the Crown Prince Yang Ji's son Bi, Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince Pei Kai's son Xian, Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Minister Director Hua Gao's son Heng were assigned to keep company with the crown prince and assist in his guidance.

value.zh: 應詹字思遠，汝南南頓人，魏侍中璩之孫也。
value.en: Ying Zhan, whose courtesy name was Siyuan, came from Nandun in Runan; he was the grandson of Ying Qu, who had served Wei as Palace Attendant.
value.literal: Ying Zhan, courtesy name Siyuan, was a native of Nandun in Runan, and a grandson of Ying Qu, Palace Attendant of Wei.

value.zh: 詹幼孤，爲祖母所養。
value.en: He lost his parents while still a boy and was brought up by his grandmother.
value.literal: In youth he was orphaned and was raised by his grandmother.

value.zh: 年十餘歲，祖母又終，居喪毀頓，杖而後起，遂以孝聞。
value.en: After his grandmother died when he was just past ten, he mourned until his body gave way and he needed a walking stick to stand; word of his filial piety spread.
value.literal: When he was a little over ten sui, his grandmother also died; in mourning he wasted away so badly that he could rise only with a staff, and he came to be known for his filial devotion.

value.zh: 家富於財，年又稚弱，乃請族人共居，委以資產，情若至親，世以此異焉。
value.en: The family was wealthy, but he was still a child; he asked his kinsmen to share one roof with him and handed his assets into their care, treating them as his nearest kin—an act that struck people of the time as extraordinary.
value.literal: His household was rich in wealth, and he was still very young, so he invited his clansmen to live together with him, entrusting them with his property; their feelings were like those of the closest kin, and the world marveled at this on that account.

value.zh: 弱冠知名，性質素弘雅，物雖犯而弗之校，以學藝文章稱。
value.en: After his capping he won a reputation; he was steady, broad-minded, and elegant by temperament, slow to take offense when others crossed him, and admired for his scholarship, arts, and writing.
value.literal: At the capping age he was already well known; by nature he was plain, magnanimous, and refined, and though things might offend him he did not contend with them; he was esteemed for learning, craft, and literary skill.

value.zh: 司徒何劭見之曰：「君子哉若人！」
value.en: When Situ He Shao met him, he exclaimed, “Here is a true gentleman.”
value.literal: Situ He Shao, seeing him, said, “What a gentleman this man is!”

value.zh: 卞壼字望之，濟陰冤句人也。
value.en: Bian Kun, style Wangzhi, was a man of Yuanju in Jiyin.
value.literal: Bian Kun, courtesy name Wangzhi, was a native of Yuanju in Jiyin.

value.zh: 祖統，琅邪內史。
value.en: His grandfather Bian Tong had been interior minister of Langya.
value.literal: His grandfather Tong was interior minister of Langya.

value.zh: 父粹，以清辯鑒察稱。
value.en: His father Bian Cui was celebrated for lucid argument and sharp discernment.
value.literal: His father Cui was famed for clear disputation and keen judgment.

value.zh: 兄弟六人並登宰府，世稱「卞氏六龍，玄仁無雙」。
value.en: Six brothers reached high ministry together; contemporaries called them “the six dragons of the Bian house, with none the equal of Xuaren.”
value.literal: Six brothers together ascended to ministerial offices; the age called them “the six dragons of the Bian clan—none matched Xuaren.”

value.zh: 玄仁，粹字也。
value.en: “Xuaren” was Bian Cui’s courtesy name.
value.literal: Xuaren was Cui’s courtesy name.

value.zh: 弟裒，嘗忤其郡將。
value.en: His brother Bian Pou once crossed the regional commander.
value.literal: His younger brother Pou once offended his commandery general.

value.zh: 郡將怒訐其門內之私，粹遂以不訓見譏議，陵遲積年。
value.en: The commander retaliated with gossip about the Bian household, so Cui was faulted for lax family discipline and languished for years.
value.literal: The commandery general angrily denounced private matters within Pou’s household, and Cui therefore came under censure as failing to instruct his family; for years he was held back.

value.zh: 惠帝初，爲尚書郎。
value.en: When Emperor Hui took the throne he entered the palace secretariat as a gentleman.
value.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Hui’s reign he became a gentleman of the Palace Secretariat.

value.zh: 楊駿執政，人多附會，而粹正直不阿。
value.en: While Yang Jun dominated the court, flatterers swarmed him; Bian Cui stayed straight and aloof.
value.literal: When Yang Jun held power, many men attached themselves to him, but Cui was upright and did not curry favor.

value.zh: 及駿誅，超拜右丞，封成陽子，稍遷至右軍將軍。
value.en: After Yang Jun fell, Cui vaulted to right secretariat aide, village marquis of Chengyang, and eventually General of the Right Army.
value.literal: When Jun was executed, Cui was abruptly promoted to right aide and enfeoffed as village marquis of Chengyang, and by stages rose to General of the Right Army.

value.zh: 張華之誅，粹以華婿免官。
value.en: When Zhang Hua died, Cui lost his post as Zhang’s son-in-law.
value.literal: At Zhang Hua’s execution, Cui was dismissed from office as Zhang Hua’s son-in-law.

value.zh: 齊王冏輔政，爲侍中、中書令，進爵爲公。
value.en: Under Prince Sima Jiong of Qi he served as palace attendant and palace secretary and was raised to a ducal fief.
value.literal: When Prince Sima Jiong of Qi assisted the government, Cui became palace attendant and palace secretary and was advanced in fief to duke.

value.zh: 及長沙王乂專權，粹立朝正色，乂忌而害之。
value.en: When Prince Sima Yi of Changsha seized power, Cui faced court with icy dignity; Yi envied him and had him killed.
value.literal: When Prince Sima Yi of Changsha monopolized power, Cui stood in court with stern dignity; Yi resented him and killed him.

value.zh: 初，粹如廁，見物若兩眼，俄而難作。
value.en: Once, relieving himself, Cui saw what looked like two eyes in the dark; soon after came his death.
value.literal: Earlier, when Cui went to the privy, he saw something like two eyes; shortly afterward the disaster occurred.

value.zh: 張軌
value.en: The subject of this biography is Zhang Gui.
value.literal: Zhang Gui.

value.zh: 張軌，字士彥，安定烏氏人，漢常山景王耳十七代孫也。
value.en: Zhang Gui, whose courtesy name was Shiyan, came from Wushi in Anding; he traced his line to Zhang Er, the Han Prince Jing of Changshan, seventeen generations back.
value.literal: Zhang Gui, courtesy name Shiyan, was a native of Wushi in Anding commandery, the seventeenth-generation descendant of Liu Er, the Prince Jing of Changshan of the Han.

value.zh: 家世孝廉，以儒學顯。
value.en: His clan had long supplied xiaolian candidates and was known for Confucian learning.
value.literal: For generations his family had produced men recommended as xiaolian, and they were eminent in Confucian scholarship.

value.zh: 父溫，為太官令。
value.en: His father Zhang Wen held the post of Director of the Imperial Kitchen.
value.literal: His father, Zhang Wen, served as Director of the Imperial Kitchen.

value.zh: 軌少明敏好學，有器望，姿儀典則，與同郡皇甫謐善，隱于宜陽女幾山。
value.en: As a young man he was bright, eager to learn, and carried an air of capacity; his deportment was exemplary. He befriended Huangfu Mi of Anding and withdrew to Mount Nüji in Yiyang.
