value.literal: In youth Gui was quick, perceptive, and fond of learning; he had presence and high repute, and his bearing was dignified and correct. He was on good terms with Huangfu Mi of the same commandery and lived in seclusion on Mount Nüji in Yiyang.

value.zh: 泰始初，受叔父錫官五品。
value.en: Early in the Taishi reign he was given fifth-rank office through his uncle Zhang Xi.
value.literal: At the beginning of the Taishi era he received from his uncle Xi an office of the fifth rank.

value.zh: 中書監張華與軌論經義及政事損益，甚器之，謂安定中正為蔽善抑才，乃美為之談，以為二品之精。
value.en: Zhang Hua, the Palace Library director, debated classical doctrine and policy with him and came to esteem him deeply, blaming Anding’s impartial judge for hiding talent and praising Zhang Gui as the outstanding man of the second-grade roster.
value.literal: Director of the Palace Library Zhang Hua discussed with him the meaning of the Classics and the gains and losses of government affairs, thought very highly of him, and said that the commandery impartial judge of Anding was concealing the worthy and suppressing talent; he therefore spoke well of him, deeming him the finest among those rated in the second grade.

value.zh: 衛將軍楊珧辟為掾，除太子舍人，累遷散騎常侍、征西軍司。
value.en: Yang Yao, General of the Guards, took him on as a clerk; he was made a gentleman attendant at the heir’s household and eventually promoted through posts to cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and western-expedition army supervisor.
value.literal: General of the Guards Yang Yao summoned him as a clerk; he was appointed Gentleman Attendant at the Heir Apparent’s Household, then rose in stages to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Army Supervisor on the Western Expedition.

value.zh: 序
value.en: Preface
value.literal: Preface

value.zh: 趙王倫篡位，署為侍中。
value.en: When Prince of Zhao Sima Lun seized the throne, Shao was named Palace Attendant.
value.literal: When Prince Zhao Lun usurped the throne, Shao was appointed Palace Attendant.

value.zh: 惠帝復阼，遂居其職。
value.en: After Emperor Hui was restored, Shao kept the same office.
value.literal: When Emperor Hui resumed the throne, Shao remained in that role.

value.zh: 司空張華為倫所誅，議者追理其事，欲復其爵，紹又駁曰：「臣之事君，當除煩去惑。
value.en: When Minister of Works Zhang Hua was put to death by Lun, some argued for restoring his titles; Shao objected again: "A minister's duty is to clear away trouble and delusion for his sovereign.
value.literal: Minister of Works Zhang Hua was executed by Lun; debaters revisited the matter and wished to restore his noble rank, but Shao again objected: "A minister serves his lord by removing confusion and distraction.

value.zh: 華歷位內外，雖粗有善事，然闔棺之責，著於遠近，兆禍始亂，華實為之。
value.en: Zhang Hua moved between palace and camp and did some good in small ways, yet his final reckoning was visible everywhere: the seeds of disaster were largely of his planting.
value.literal: Hua held posts inside and outside the court; though he had some decent deeds, the blame that closes the coffin was plain far and near—the omens that began the calamity were really his doing.

value.zh: 故鄭討幽公之亂，斫子家之棺；
value.en: So Zheng, punishing Duke You of Lu's rebellion, split minister Zijia's coffin open with an axe.
value.literal: Hence when Zheng punished the turmoil of Duke You, they hacked open Zijia's coffin;

value.zh: 魯戮隱罪，終篇貶翬。
value.en: Lu executed Guan Yin for his crime, and the Spring and Autumn closes by censuring Hui.
value.literal: Lu executed Yin for his guilt, and the classic ends by censuring Hui.

value.zh: 未忍重戮，事已弘矣，謂不宜復其爵位，理其無罪。」
value.en: I will not press for harsher punishment than death; the case is already settled. Restoring his titles or declaring him blameless would be wrong."
value.literal: I cannot bear to urge heavier punishment; the matter is already broad enough—I say his rank should not be restored nor his innocence proclaimed."

value.zh: 時帝初反正，紹又上疏曰：「臣聞改前轍者則車不傾，革往弊者則政不爽。
value.en: With the emperor newly restored, Shao submitted another memorial: "They say that straightening the wheel tracks keeps the carriage upright, and curing old abuses keeps government true.
value.literal: At the time the emperor had just been restored; Shao further submitted a memorial: "I have heard that those who correct the rut keep the cart from tipping; those who mend past abuses keep government sound.

value.zh: 太一統于元首，百司役於多士，故周文興于上，成康穆於下也。
value.en: The supreme pivot sits with the ruler; every ministry depends on capable men—thus King Wen flourished on high while kings Cheng and Kang enjoyed peace below.
value.literal: The Grand Unity rests in the sovereign's head; myriad offices labor through many officers—thus King Wen rose above and Cheng and Kang were tranquil below.

value.zh: 存不忘亡，《易》之善義；
value.en: The Changes teaches us to remember peril even in safety—
value.literal: To remember survival amid peril is the fine meaning of the Changes;

value.zh: 願陛下無忘金墉，大司馬無忘潁上，大將軍無忘黃橋，則禍亂之萌無由而兆矣。」
value.en: May Your Majesty remember the fortress at Jinyong; may the Grand Marshal remember Yingshang; may the Grand General remember Huang Bridge—then the seeds of calamity will never sprout."
value.literal: I pray Your Majesty will not forget Jinyong; the Grand Marshal will not forget Yingshang; the Grand General will not forget Huang Bridge—then the sprouts of disaster will have nowhere to arise."

value.zh: 劉沈，字道真，燕國薊人也。
value.en: Liu Shen, courtesy name Daozhen, came from Ji in Yan.
value.literal: Liu Shen, courtesy name Daozhen, was a man of Ji in the state of Yan.

value.zh: 世為北州名族。
value.en: His clan ranked among the north's great families for generations.
value.literal: For generations his clan was a distinguished house of the northern provinces.

value.zh: 少仕州郡，博學好古。
value.en: Youth brought minor provincial posts; he read widely and revered antiquity.
value.literal: In youth he served in provincial posts; he was broadly learned and loved antiquity.

value.zh: 太保衛瓘辟為掾，領本邑大中正。
value.en: Grand Mentor Wei Guan took him on as an aide and put him in charge of local personnel appraisal as senior rectifier.
value.literal: Grand Mentor Wei Guan summoned him as aide and assigned him concurrent duty as senior rectifier for his native district.

value.zh: 敦儒道，愛賢能，進霍原為二品，及申理張華，皆辭旨明峻，為當時所稱。
value.en: He championed scholarship, prized talent, promoted Huo Yuan to the second grade, and defended Zhang Hua—each memorial lucid and uncompromising, earning wide acclaim.
value.literal: He honored Confucian teaching and loved worthy talent; advancing Huo Yuan to the second rank and arguing Zhang Hua's case—all were marked by bright, stern wording and praised by contemporaries.

value.zh: 齊王冏輔政，引為左長史，遷侍中。
value.en: Prince of Qi Sima Jiong, while directing government, brought Liu Shen in as Left Senior Clerk and soon promoted him to Palace Attendant.
value.literal: When Prince of Qi Sima Jiong directed affairs, he summoned Shen as Left Senior Clerk and promoted him to Palace Attendant.

value.zh: 于時李流亂蜀，詔沈以侍中、假節，統益州刺史羅尚、梁州刺史許雄等以討流。
value.en: While Li Liu ravaged Shu, the throne named Liu Shen Palace Attendant with credential staff to coordinate Luo Shang of Yi Province, Xu Xiong of Liang Province, and others against him.
value.literal: At that time Li Liu rebelled in Shu; an edict appointed Shen as Palace Attendant with credential staff to oversee Inspector of Yi Province Luo Shang, Inspector of Liang Province Xu Xiong, and others to strike Liu.

value.zh: 行次長安，河間王顒請留沉為軍司，遣席薳代之。
value.en: His march paused at Chang'an; Prince of Hejian Sima Yong asked to keep Liu Shen as army marshal and dispatched Xi Yuan to replace him on campaign.
value.literal: Marching, he halted at Chang'an; Prince of Hejian Yong requested to retain Shen as army marshal and sent Xi Yuan to replace him.

value.zh: 後領雍州刺史。
value.en: He later added concurrent duty as Inspector of Yong Province.
value.literal: Later he concurrently served as Inspector of Yong Province.

value.zh: 及張昌作亂，詔顒遣沉將州兵萬人並征西府五千人，自藍田關以討之，顒不奉詔。
value.en: When Zhang Chang rose, an edict told Yong to send Liu Shen with ten thousand Yong troops and five thousand western expedition troops through Lantian Pass—Yong ignored it.
value.literal: When Zhang Chang rebelled, an edict ordered Yong to send Shen leading ten thousand provincial troops plus five thousand from the western expedition headquarters through Lantian Pass to attack him; Yong did not obey the edict.

value.zh: 沉自領州兵至藍田，顒又逼奪其眾。
value.en: Liu Shen drove the provincial army to Lantian anyway; Yong seized those troops from him.
value.literal: Shen himself led provincial troops to Lantian; Yong again pressed and seized his forces.

value.zh: 長沙王乂命沉將武吏四百人還州。
value.en: Prince of Changsha Sima Yi ordered Liu Shen to march four hundred armed clerks back to Yong Province.
value.literal: Prince of Changsha Yi ordered Shen to lead four hundred martial clerks back to the province.

value.zh: 韋忠字子節，平陽人也。
value.en: Wei Zhong, courtesy name Zijie, came from Pingyang.
value.literal: Wei Zhong, courtesy name Zijie, was a man of Pingyang.

value.zh: 少慷慨，有不可奪之志。
value.en: From youth he burned with principle nothing could break.
value.literal: From youth he was impassioned and had an unshakeable will.

value.zh: 好學博通，性不虛諾。
value.en: He read widely and kept every pledge.
value.literal: He loved learning and was broadly conversant; by nature he did not make empty promises.

value.zh: 閉門修己，不交當世，每至吉凶，親表贈遺，一無所受。
value.en: He shut his gate, shunned fashion, and refused every gift from kin at weddings or funerals.
value.literal: He closed his gate and cultivated himself, did not mingle with contemporaries; whenever kin came with gifts for auspicious or inauspicious occasions he accepted nothing.

value.zh: 年十二，喪父，哀慕毀悴，杖而後起。
value.en: At twelve he buried his father—grief wasted him until he needed a cane to rise.
value.literal: At twelve he lost his father; he mourned in grief emaciation and needed a staff to rise.

value.zh: 司空裴秀吊之，匍匐號訴，哀慟感人。
value.en: Minister Pei Xiu condoled—Zhong crawled forward wailing until listeners wept.
value.literal: Minister of Works Pei Xiu condoled with him; he crawled and wailed his grievance—his grief moved others.

value.zh: 秀出而告人曰：「此子長大必為佳器。」
value.en: Pei Xiu left saying: "This boy will be worthy timber grown."
value.literal: Xiu went out and told people: "This boy when grown will surely become fine timber."

value.zh: 歸而命子頠造焉。
value.en: He sent his son Pei Yi to call.
value.literal: On returning he ordered his son Yi to visit him.

value.zh: 服闋，遂廬於墓所。
value.en: When mourning ended he built a hut at his father's tomb.
value.literal: When mourning ended he therefore built a hut at the tomb site.

value.zh: 頠慕而造之，皆托行不見。
value.en: Pei Yi admired him and visited twice—Zhong pleaded errands and refused audience.
value.literal: Yi admired him and went to visit—both times Zhong pleaded absence and did not see him.

value.zh: 家貧，藜藿不充，人不堪其憂，而忠不改其樂。
value.en: His house knew hunger—wild greens barely filled the bowl—others would despair; Zhong stayed content.
value.literal: His household was poor—wild greens scarcely enough—others could not endure such sorrow yet Zhong did not alter his joy.

value.zh: 頠為僕射，數言之于司空張華，華辟之，辭疾不起。
value.en: When Pei Yi rose to Vice Director he praised Zhong to Zhang Hua—Zhang summoned him but Zhong pleaded illness.
value.literal: When Yi became Vice Director, he repeatedly spoke of Zhong to Minister of Works Zhang Hua; Hua summoned him—Zhong declined illness and did not rise.

value.zh: 人問其故，忠曰：「吾茨簷賤士，本無宦情。
value.en: Asked why, he said: "I am a nobody under a thatched eaves—no taste for office.
value.literal: People asked his reason; Zhong said: "I am a mean scholar under a thatched roof—originally without appetite for office.

value.zh: 且茂先華而不實，裴頠欲而無厭，棄典禮而附賊後，若此，豈大丈夫之所宜行邪！
value.en: Moreover Zhang Hua blooms without fruit; Pei Yi covets without limit—they betray ritual and cling to usurpers—what worthy man would walk that road!
value.literal: Moreover Maoxian is flowery without substance; Pei Yi desires without satiety—they abandon canonical rites and attach themselves to villain successors—with conduct like this, how could it be fitting for a great man!

value.zh: 裴常有心托我，常恐洪濤蕩岳，餘波見漂，況可臨尾閭而窺沃焦哉！」
value.en: Pei Yi keeps pressing his patronage—I dread tidal waves that bury mountains and folk tossed on the backwash; why would I cling to the cosmic drain or stare into the burning shoal?"
value.literal: Pei Yi has always wished to patronize me; I always feared great billows would scour the peaks and survivors drift on the wake—how much more dare I cling to Weilu's torrent and peek at Wojiao's shoals!"

value.zh: 太守陳楚迫為功曹。
value.en: Prefect Chen Chu forced him into the merit-evaluator post.
value.literal: Administrator Chen Chu compelled him to serve as merit evaluator.

value.zh: 會山羌破郡，楚攜子出走，賊射之，中三創。
value.en: Mountain Qiang raiders shattered the district; Chu fled with his son until bandits shot them three times.
value.literal: When Shanqiang tribes smashed the commandery, Chu fled carrying his son—the bandits shot them and struck three wounds.

value.zh: 忠冒刃伏楚。
value.en: Zhong threw himself onto Chu beneath the blades.
value.literal: Zhong braved blades to shield Chu.

value.zh: 以身捍之，泣曰：「韋忠願以身代君，乞諸君哀之。」
value.en: Covering Chu with his body he wept: "Take me instead—spare him."
value.literal: Using his body to defend him, weeping he said: "Wei Zhong wishes to substitute body for lord—I beg you gentlemen pity him."

value.zh: 亦遭五矢。
value.en: Five shafts struck him as well.
value.literal: He also suffered five arrows.

value.zh: 賊相謂曰：「義士也！」
value.en: The bandits murmured: "A true righteous man!"
value.literal: The bandits said to each other: "A man of principle!"

value.zh: 舍之。
value.en: They let them go.
value.literal: They released him.

value.zh: 忠於是負楚以歸。
value.en: Zhong bore Chu home across his shoulders.
value.literal: Zhong therefore carried Chu on his back home.

value.zh: 後仕劉聰，為鎮西大將軍，平羌校尉，討叛羌，矢盡，不屈節而死。
value.en: Under Liu Cong he became Grand General Who Guards the West and Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang—fighting rebel Qiang until his arrows failed, he died unbroken.
value.literal: Later he served Liu Cong as Grand General Who Guards the West and Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang; campaigning against rebel Qiang he exhausted his arrows and died without yielding his integrity.

value.zh: 若夫穹昊垂景，少微以躔其次；
value.en: Consider how the high heavens let fall their light, and the hermit star Shaowei keeps to its station in the sky.
value.literal: As for the vaulted heaven lowering its radiance, Shaowei thereby treads its place among them;

value.zh: 《文》《系》探幽，貞遁以成其象。
value.en: The "Appended Remarks" and "Wings" sound out what lies in shadow, and the hexagram of principled retreat gives that stance its perfect emblem.
value.literal: The "Wen" and "Xi" plumb the hidden; steadfast withdrawal completes their image.

value.zh: 故有避於言色，其道聞乎孔公；
value.en: Hence men who gave nothing away in word or look, whose path we know because Confucius spoke of them;
value.literal: Therefore there were those who avoided it in speech and countenance; of their way one hears from the Duke Kong;

value.zh: 驕乎富貴，厥義詳于孫子。
value.en: and the proud scorning of wealth and station, whose moral sense Sunzi laid out at length.
value.literal: As for pride toward wealth and noble rank, its meaning was set forth in detail by Master Sun.

value.zh: 是以處柔伊存，有生之恆性；
value.en: To hold to yielding strength is how life endures; that is the fixed temper of everything that breathes;
value.literal: Therefore to abide in softness is how it endures; it is the constant nature of the living;

value.zh: 在盈斯害，惟神之常道。
value.en: while fullness invites injury—such has always been heaven's steady law.
value.literal: to be at fullness is thereby harm; it is the constant way of the spirit.

value.zh: 古先智士體其若茲，介焉超俗，浩然養素，藏聲江海之上，卷跡囂氛之表，漱流而激其清，寢巢而韜其耀，良畫以符其志，絕機以虛其心。
value.en: Men of old who grasped this truth stood aloof from the crowd, breathed in a clarity that nourished plain living, let their names die away beyond the rivers and seas, and withdrew their footsteps from the world's noise. They drank from running water to keep themselves clean, dwelt like birds in the wild to dim their luster, chose their course with deliberate care, and stilled every scheme so the heart could rest empty.
value.literal: Ancient wise men embodied it thus: standing apart they transcended the vulgar, in vast purity they nurtured simplicity, they hid their voices above the rivers and seas, they rolled up their traces beyond the clamor and dust, they rinsed their mouths in the current to quicken its clearness, they slept in nests to sheathe their brilliance, they took fine plans to match their intent, they cut off contrivance to empty their hearts.

value.zh: 玉輝冰潔，川渟岳峙，修至樂之道，固無疆之休，長往邈而不追，安排窅而無悶，修身自保，悔吝弗生，詩人《考槃》之歌，抑在茲矣。
value.en: They shone like jade and held the chill of ice; they were still as a held river, steadfast as a mountain. They walked the path of deepest contentment and won a peace without end. Once they had gone far, none could overtake them; they accepted whatever came, untroubled in the dark. Guarding the person, they kept harm away—no cause for remorse—and the ode the Classic of Poetry calls "Kao pan" might almost have been written of them.
value.literal: Jade radiance, ice purity; like a river at rest, like a peak standing; they cultivated the way of supreme joy, they secured boundless good fortune; long gone, remote, none could pursue them; settled in the depths, without vexation; they cultivated the self to preserve themselves, regret and shame did not arise—the poet's song of "Kao pan," is it not here?

value.zh: 至於體天作制之後，訟息刑清之時，尚乃仄席幽貞以康神化，徵聘之禮賁於岩穴，玉帛之贄委於窒衡，故《月令》曰：「季春之月聘名士，禮賢者」，斯之謂歟！
value.en: Even once a ruler had aligned his government with heaven and the courts fell quiet, he would still leave the high seat half-empty for recluses of firm integrity, so culture might flourish. Envoys climbed to mountain huts; jade and silk waited on the doorsteps of the poor. That is why the "Monthly Ordinances" says that in late spring one should call forth noted scholars and honor the wise—surely it speaks of just such a time.
value.literal: As for after one embodied heaven and established institutions, at the time when lawsuits ceased and punishments were clear, still one vacated the mat for the hidden and steadfast to perfect spiritual transformation; the rites of summons and appointment shone into cliffside caves, gifts of jade and silk piled at humble doors—therefore the "Monthly Ordinances" says, "In the last month of spring one hires eminent scholars and treats the worthy with ritual"—does it not mean this?

value.zh: 自典午運開，旁求隱逸，譙元彥之杜絕人事，江思悛之嘯詠林藪，峻其貞白之軌，成其出塵之跡，雖不應其嘉招，亦足激其貪競。
value.en: Since the house of Jin rose, the throne has combed the hills for hidden men: Qiao Xiu shut his gate on the world, Jiang Dun whistled and sang deep in the hills. They raised the standard of unstained integrity and showed how to step outside the scramble for power. They never took the court's gracious offers, yet their example was enough to shame the grasping and the ambitious.
value.literal: From when the Jin fortune opened, seeking far and wide for recluses, as with Qiao Xiuyuan's cutting off human affairs, or Jiang Silun's whistling and chanting in woods and marshes, they made steep the track of chastity and purity, they completed traces beyond the dust; although they did not respond to fine summons, still it was enough to sting greed and rivalry.

value.zh: 今美其高尚之德，綴集於篇。
value.en: Here I gather their stories to honor the height of their character.
value.literal: Now I praise their lofty virtue and string them together in this chapter.

value.zh: 喬好學不倦。
value.en: Qiao never wearied of books.
value.literal: Qiao loved learning and did not tire.

value.zh: 父粲陽狂不言，喬與二弟並棄學業，絕人事，侍疾家庭，至粲沒，足不出邑里。
value.en: When his father feigned madness and silence, Qiao and his two brothers quit school, shut out the world, and nursed him until he died—never leaving their hamlet in all those years.
value.literal: When his father Can feigned madness and would not speak, Qiao with his two younger brothers abandoned their studies, cut off human affairs, and nursed the illness in the household until Can died, not stepping beyond the village.

value.zh: 司隸校尉劉毅嘗抗論於朝廷曰：「使范武威疾若不篤，是為伯夷、叔齊復存於今。
value.en: Liu Yi once told the court, "If Governor Fan's sickness is feigned, then Bo Yi and Shu Qi walk among us again.
value.literal: Metropolitan Governor Liu Yi once spoke bluntly at court, saying, "If Fan Wuwei's illness is not grave, then Bo Yi and Shu Qi live again today.

value.zh: 如其信篤，益是聖主所宜哀矜。
value.en: If it is genuine, a sage king should pity him all the more.
value.literal: If it is truly grave, all the more is it what a sage ruler ought to pity.

value.zh: 其子久侍父疾，名德著茂，不加敘用，深為朝廷惜遺賢之譏也。」
value.en: The sons have served a sick father for years with shining virtue; to leave them unranked is to invite the charge that the throne wastes good men."
value.literal: His sons have long attended a father's sickness; their fame and virtue shine bright—failure to employ them is a reproach the court will bear for wasting worthies."

value.zh: 元康中，詔求廉讓沖退覆道寒素者，不計資，以參選敘。
value.en: Under Yuankang the throne sought modest scholars of cold pedigree, rank no object.
value.literal: In the Yuankang period an edict sought men who were honest, yielding, retiring, and covered the Way in humble plainness, without regard to seniority, to be entered in selection.

value.zh: 尚書郎王琨乃薦喬曰：「喬稟德真粹，立操高潔，儒學精深，含章內奧，安貧樂道，棲志窮巷，簞瓢詠業，長而彌堅，誠當今之寒素，著厲俗之清彥。」
value.en: Palace gentleman Wang Kun recommended him: pure in endowment, high in principle, steeped in the canon yet inward-turned, happy in poverty and fixed in purpose—"the very cold-clad scholar the age needs."
value.literal: Gentleman of the palace Wang Kun then recommended Qiao, saying, "Qiao is endowed with virtue true and pure, established in conduct lofty and clean, deep in Confucian learning, holding pattern within, content with poverty and joyful in the Way, lodging his intent in a poor lane, with basket and gourd chanting his occupation—longer yet more firm—truly the cold plainness of today, a clear paragon to brace vulgar ways."

value.zh: 時張華領司徒，天下所舉凡十七人，于喬特發優論。
value.en: Zhang Hua presided over the ministry; seventeen names came up from the realm, but only Qiao drew a special encomium.
value.literal: At the time Zhang Hua headed the ministry of education; of all the empire's nominees seventeen were listed, and for Qiao alone a superior appraisal was issued.

value.zh: 又吏部郎郗隆亦思求海內幽遁之士，喬供養衡門，至於白首，於是除樂安令。
value.en: Personnel director Xi Long also combed for hidden talent; learning that Qiao had kept his parents in a lane of wattles until their hair turned white, the court named him magistrate of Le'an.
value.literal: Also personnel director Xi Long wished to seek recluses within the seas; Qiao supported his parents at a brushwood gate until hoary age—thereupon he was appointed magistrate of Le'an.

value.zh: 辭疾不拜。
value.en: He pleaded illness and never went.
value.literal: He pleaded illness and did not take up the post.

value.zh: 喬凡一舉孝廉，八薦公府，再舉清白異行，又舉寒素，一無所就。
value.en: He was nominated once as filial-incorrupt, eight times to the Three Ducal Offices, twice for outstanding purity, once again for cold pedigree—and never accepted.
value.literal: Qiao in all was once recommended filial and incorrupt, eight times recommended to the ducal offices, twice recommended for unsullied conduct out of the ordinary, and again recommended for cold plainness—he took none of them.

value.zh: 魯勝，字叔時，代郡人也。
value.en: Lu Sheng, courtesy name Shushi, came from Dai commandery.
value.literal: Lu Sheng, styled Shushi, was a man of Dai commandery.

value.zh: 少有才操，為佐著作郎。
value.en: Young, able, and principled, he became assistant editorialist.
value.literal: In youth he had talent and integrity, and served as assistant editorialist.

value.zh: 元康初，遷建康令。
value.en: Early in Yuankang he was named magistrate of Jiankang.
value.literal: At the beginning of Yuankang he was moved to magistrate of Jiankang.

value.zh: 到官，著《正天論》云：「以冬至之後立晷測影，准度日月星。
value.en: On taking office he wrote a treatise called "Setting Heaven Right," arguing that from the winter solstice one should set a gnomon and read shadows to calibrate sun, moon, and stars.
value.literal: Arriving at office, he composed the "Correcting Heaven Treatise," saying, "After the winter solstice set a gnomon and measure shadow to gauge sun, moon, and stars.

value.zh: 臣案日月裁徑百里，無千里；
value.en: He maintained that sun and moon span only a hundred leagues, not a thousand;
value.literal: Your subject investigates: sun and moon are only a hundred li across, not a thousand li;

value.zh: 星十里，不百里。」
value.en: and stars ten leagues, not a hundred."
value.literal: stars ten li, not a hundred li."

value.zh: 遂表上求下群公卿士考論。
value.en: He tabled the essay and begged the high ministers to debate it.
value.literal: Thereupon he submitted a memorial asking that it be sent down for the assembled dukes, ministers, and gentlemen to examine and debate.

value.zh: 「若臣言合理，當得改先代之失，而正天地之紀。
value.en: "If I speak with reason," he wrote, "let the court mend the mistakes of earlier calendars and set heaven's pattern straight.
value.literal: "If your subject's words accord with reason, then let him amend the errors of former ages and set right the pattern of heaven and earth.

value.zh: 如無據驗，甘即刑戮，以彰虛妄之罪。」
value.en: If I cannot prove my case, I will gladly die to show the world I was a fraud."
value.literal: If there is no supporting verification, I willingly accept execution at once to expose the crime of empty falsehood."

value.zh: 事遂不報。
value.en: The throne never answered.
value.literal: The matter in the end received no reply.

value.zh: 嘗歲日望氣，知將來多故，便稱疾去官。
value.en: Watching the year's omens at New Year he foresaw chaos and resigned on grounds of illness.
value.literal: On New Year's Day he once observed vapors and knew that coming years would bring much turmoil; then he pleaded illness and left office.

value.zh: 中書令張華遣子勸其更仕，再徵博士，舉中書郎，皆不就。
value.en: Zhang Hua sent his son to coax him back; twice the court called him as erudite and nominated him palace secretary—he refused each time.
value.literal: Director Zhang Hua sent his son to urge him to take office again; twice he was summoned as erudite and recommended as palace secretary—he took none of them.

value.zh: 霍原，字休明，燕國廣陽人也。
value.en: Huo Yuan, courtesy name Xiuming, was from Guangyang in Yan.
value.literal: Huo Yuan, styled Xiuming, was a man of Guangyang in the state of Yan.

value.zh: 少有志力，叔父坐法當死，原入獄訟之，楚毒備加，終免叔父。
value.en: While still young he took tortures in prison to save an uncle condemned to die.
value.literal: In youth he had determination and strength; his uncle by law of a crime deserved death, Yuan entered prison to plead the case, full torture was applied, and in the end he spared his uncle.

value.zh: 年十八，觀太學行禮，因留習之。
value.en: At eighteen he watched the academy rites and stayed to master them.
value.literal: At eighteen he watched the Grand Academy perform rites and therefore stayed to practice them.

value.zh: 貴游子弟聞而重之，欲與相見，以其名微，不欲晝往，乃夜共造焉。
value.en: Great lords' sons respected him but thought his name too slight for a daylight call, so they came by torchlight.
value.literal: Sons of the nobility heard and esteemed him, wishing to meet him; because his name was lowly they did not wish to go by day, so together they visited him by night.

value.zh: 父友同郡劉岱將舉之，未果而病篤，臨終，敕其子沈曰：「霍原慕道清虛，方成奇器，汝後必薦之。」
value.en: Liu Dai, his father's friend, meant to sponsor him but died first, telling his son Shen, 'Huo Yuan is a vessel in the making—remember to lift him up.'
value.literal: His father's friend Liu Dai of the same commandery was about to recommend him, but without result fell gravely ill; at the point of death he charged his son Shen, saying, "Huo Yuan loves the Way, clear and empty; he will become a rare vessel—you must recommend him later."

value.zh: 後歸鄉里。
value.en: Later Yuan went home to the hills.
value.literal: Later he returned to his home village.

value.zh: 高陽許猛素服其名，會為幽州刺史，將詣之，主簿當車諫不可出界，猛歎恨而止。
value.en: Governor Xu Meng of Gaoyang meant to call on him until his clerk barred a governor from crossing the line—Meng gave up with a sigh.
value.literal: Xu Meng of Gaoyang had long admired his name; when he became governor of Youzhou he meant to visit him, but his chief clerk remonstrated from the cart that he could not go beyond the border, and Meng sighed with regret and desisted.

value.zh: 原山居積年，門徒百數，燕王月致羊酒。
value.en: He taught a hundred disciples in the hills while the prince of Yan sent monthly sheep and wine.
value.literal: Yuan dwelt in the mountains many years; disciples numbered in the hundreds; the prince of Yan monthly sent sheep and wine.

value.zh: 及劉沈為國大中正，元康中，進原為二品，司徒不過，沈乃上表理之。
value.en: Liu Shen ranked him second class; the ministry of education balked until Shen memorialized again.
value.literal: When Liu Shen became grand impartial and just for the state, in Yuankang he advanced Yuan to second rank; the minister of education would not pass it, so Shen submitted a memorial to argue the case.

value.zh: 詔下司徒參論，中書監張華令陳准奏為上品，詔可。
value.en: Zhang Hua had Chen Zhun move him to the top grade, and the throne agreed.
value.literal: An edict ordered the minister of education to deliberate jointly; director Zhang Hua ordered Chen Zhun to memorialize him as highest grade, and the edict approved.

value.zh: 元康末，原與王褒等俱以賢良徵，累下州郡，以禮發遣，皆不到。
value.en: Late in Yuankang he was summoned with Wang Bao as a worthy; the counties escorted him with full rites and he still would not go.
value.literal: At the end of Yuankang, Yuan with Wang Bao and others was summoned as worthy and good; repeatedly the commandery was ordered to dispatch him with ritual, and each time he did not arrive.

value.zh: 後王浚稱制謀僭，使人問之，原不答，浚心銜之。
value.en: When Wang Jun seized the government and sounded him out, Yuan stayed silent, and Jun nursed a grudge.
value.literal: Later Wang Jun seized power and plotted usurpation; he sent men to ask him, and Yuan did not answer; Jun harbored resentment.

value.zh: 又有遼東囚徒三百餘人，依山為賊，意欲劫原為主事，亦未行。
value.en: Three hundred Liaodong fugitives in the hills wanted him for chieftain but never acted.
value.literal: Moreover more than three hundred convicts of Liaodong, relying on the mountains as bandits, wished to seize Yuan to be their leader, but also did not carry it out.

value.zh: 時有謠曰：「天子在何許？
value.en: A children's rhyme asked, 'Where sits the Son of Heaven?
value.literal: At the time a rhyme said, "Where is the Son of Heaven?

value.zh: 近在豆田中。」
value.en: In the bean patch just ahead.'
value.literal: Near at hand in the bean field."

value.zh: 浚以豆為霍，收原斬之，懸其首。
value.en: Wang Jun read bean as Huo, seized Yuan, beheaded him, and spiked his head.
value.literal: Jun took bean as Huo and seized Yuan and executed him, hanging up his head.

value.zh: 諸生悲哭，夜竊屍共埋殯之。
value.en: His students stole the body by night and gave him burial.
value.literal: The students wept in grief; by night they stole the corpse and together buried it.

value.zh: 遠近駭愕，莫不冤痛之。
value.en: The realm cried injustice.
value.literal: Far and near were shocked; none did not feel him wronged.

value.zh: 慕容廆
value.en: Murong Hui
value.literal: Murong Hui

value.zh: 廆幼而魁岸，美姿貌，身長八尺，雄傑有大度。
value.en: Even young he stood eight chi tall—striking, heroic, broad.
value.literal: From youth Hui was imposing and handsome, eight chi tall, heroic and magnanimous.

value.zh: 安北將軍張華雅有知人之鑒，廆童丱時往謁之，華甚歎異，謂曰：「君至長必為命世之器，匡難濟時者也。」
value.en: Zhang Hua said, "When you grow up you will be an instrument for the age—one who rectifies disaster and aids the times."
value.literal: General Who Pacifies the North Zhang Hua was famed for judging men; while still a boy Hui visited him. Hua marveled and said, "When grown you will be an instrument for the age—one who rectifies disaster and aids the times."

value.zh: 因以所服簪幘遺廆，結殷勤而別。
value.en: He gave Hui his cap pin and turban as farewell gifts.
value.literal: Thereupon he gave Hui his own hairpin and turban as gifts and parted with earnest warmth.

value.zh: 涉歸死，其弟耐篡位，將謀殺廆，廆亡潛以避禍。
value.en: Uncle Nai seized power and hunted him until kinsmen restored Hui.
value.literal: When Shegui died, his younger brother Nai seized the throne and plotted to murder Hui; Hui fled into hiding to escape harm.

value.zh: 後國人殺耐，迎廆立之。
value.en: The tribe slew Nai and enthroned Hui.
value.literal: Later the tribes killed Nai and welcomed Hui to the throne.

value.zh: 褚遂良 韓瑗 來濟 上官儀
value.en: Chu Suiliang, Han Yuan, Lai Ji, and Shang Guanyi
value.literal: Chu Suiliang, Han Yuan, Lai Ji, Shang Guanyi

value.zh: 疏奏，帝謂瑗曰：「遂良之情，朕亦知之矣。
value.en: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor told Yuan, "I also know Suiliang's feelings.
value.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor told Yuan: "Suiliang's feeling—I also know it.

value.zh: 然其悖戾犯上，以此責之，朕豈有過，卿言何若是之深也！」
value.en: Yet he was perverse and violent in offending his superiors. For this he is blamed. How could I be at fault? Why are your words so extreme!"
value.literal: Yet his perversity and violence offended superiors—for this he is blamed. How could I have fault? Why are your words so deep as this!"

value.zh: 瑗對曰：「遂良可謂社稷忠臣，臣恐以諛佞之輩，蒼蠅點白，損陷忠貞。
value.en: Yuan replied, "Suiliang can be called a loyal minister of the altars of state. I fear that flatterers and sycophants, like flies spotting white cloth, will harm and trap the loyal and upright.
value.literal: Yuan replied: "Suiliang can be called a loyal minister of the altars of state. I fear that with flatterers and sycophants, blue flies spotting white, the loyal and upright will be harmed and trapped.

value.zh: 昔微子去之而殷國以亡，張華不死而綱紀不亂，國之慾謝，善人其衰。
value.en: Formerly when Weizi left, the Yin state perished; when Zhang Hua did not die, institutions and law were not disordered. When a state is about to decline, good men decay with it.
value.literal: Formerly when Weizi left, the Yin state thereby perished; when Zhang Hua did not die, institutions and law were not disordered—a state about to decline, good men thereby decay.

value.zh: 今陛下富有四海，八紘清泰，忽驅逐舊臣，而不垂省察乎！
value.en: Now Your Majesty possesses the four seas and the eight cords are clear and peaceful. Will you suddenly drive out old ministers and not extend examination and consideration!
value.literal: Now Your Majesty possesses the four seas, the eight cords clear and peaceful—suddenly driving out old ministers, yet not extending examination and consideration!

value.zh: 伏願違彼覆車，以收往過，垂勸誡於事君，則群生幸甚。」
value.en: I beg you to avoid that overturned cart, recover from former excess, and hang admonition on serving the ruler. Then the myriad living would be greatly fortunate."
value.literal: I prostrate myself wishing to avoid that overturned cart, to recover former excess, to hang admonition on serving the ruler—then the myriad living would be greatly fortunate."

value.zh: 帝竟不納。
value.en: The emperor in the end did not accept it.
value.literal: The Emperor in the end did not accept it.

value.zh: 瑗以言不見用，憂憤上表，請歸田裡，詔不許。
value.en: Because his words were not employed, Yuan in worry and anger submitted a memorial requesting to return to his fields and village, but the edict did not permit it.
value.literal: Yuan because his words were not employed, in worry and anger submitted a memorial requesting to return to his fields and village—the edict did not permit it.

value.zh: 顯慶二年，許敬宗、李義府希皇后之旨，誣奏瑗與褚遂良潛謀不軌，以桂州用武之地，故授遂良桂州刺史，實以為外援。
value.en: In 657 Xu Jingzong and Li Yifu, hoping to please the empress, falsely memorialized that Yuan and Chu Suiliang had secretly plotted treason. Because Guizhou was a place of military importance, Suiliang had been made Prefect of Guizhou in reality to serve as external support.
value.literal: In the second year of Xianqing, Xu Jingzong and Li Yifu hoping for the empress's intent falsely memorialized that Yuan and Chu Suiliang secretly plotted irregularity—because Guizhou was a place of military use, therefore Suiliang was granted Prefect of Guizhou, in reality to serve as external aid.

value.zh: 於是更貶遂良為愛州刺史，左授瑗振州刺史。
value.en: Thereupon Suiliang was again demoted to Prefect of Aizhou, and Yuan was demoted to Prefect of Zhenzhou.
value.literal: Thereupon Suiliang was again demoted to Prefect of Aizhou, and Yuan was demoted left to Prefect of Zhenzhou.

value.zh: 四年，卒官，年五十四。
value.en: In 659 he died in office at the age of fifty-four.
value.literal: In the fourth year he died in office, age fifty-four.

value.zh: 明年，長孫無忌死，敬宗等又奏瑗與無忌通謀，遣使殺之。
value.en: The next year Zhangsun Wuji died. Jingzong and others again memorialized that Yuan had communicated plots with Wuji and sent envoys to kill him.
value.literal: The next year Zhangsun Wuji died; Jingzong and others again memorialized that Yuan had communicated plots with Wuji and sent envoys to kill him.

value.zh: 及使至，瑗已死，更發棺驗屍而還，籍沒其家，孫配徙嶺表。
value.en: When the envoy arrived, Yuan was already dead. They opened the coffin and examined the corpse and returned, registered and confiscated his household, and his grandsons were sentenced to exile beyond the Ling range.
value.literal: When the envoy arrived, Yuan was already dead; they again opened the coffin and examined the corpse and returned, registered and confiscated his household, and grandsons were sentenced to exile beyond the Ling range.

value.zh: 神龍元年，則天遺制令復其官爵。
value.en: In 705 Empress Zetian's testamentary institution ordered restoration of his offices and titles.
value.literal: In the first year of Shenlong, Empress Zetian's testamentary institution ordered restoration of his offices and titles.

value.zh: 《易》曰：「有天地然後有萬物，有萬物然後有男女，有男女然後有夫婦。」
value.en: The Book of Changes says: "Once heaven and earth exist, the myriad things follow; once the myriad things exist, male and female follow; once male and female exist, husband and wife follow."
value.literal: The Book of Changes says: "When there are heaven and earth, then there are the myriad things; when there are the myriad things, then there are male and female; when there are male and female, then there are husband and wife."

value.zh: 夫婦之義尚矣哉！
value.en: How exalted is the meaning of husband and wife!
value.literal: The meaning of husband and wife—how exalted it is!

value.zh: 周禮，王者立后六宮，三夫人、九嬪、二十七世婦、八十一御妻，以聽天下之內治。
value.en: The Rites of Zhou say the king set up an empress and six inner palaces—three consorts, nine concubines, twenty-seven palace ladies, and eighty-one attendants—to govern affairs within the realm.
value.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, the king established the empress and the six inner palaces—three consorts, nine imperial concubines, twenty-seven palace ladies, and eighty-one palace attendants—to oversee inner governance throughout the realm.

value.zh: 故《昏義》云：「天子之與后，猶日之與月，陰之與陽，相須而成者也。」
value.en: So the "Meaning of Marriage" says the Son of Heaven and the empress are like sun and moon, yin and yang, completing one another.
value.literal: Hence the "Meaning of Marriage" says: "The Son of Heaven and the empress are like sun and moon, yin and yang—they need each other to be complete."

value.zh: 漢初因秦稱號，帝母稱皇太后，后稱皇后，而加以美人、良人、八子、七子之屬。
value.en: Early Han kept Qin titles: the emperor's mother was empress dowager, his consort empress, with further ranks of beauty, good person, eighth son, seventh son, and the like.
value.literal: At the beginning of Han, titles followed Qin usage: the emperor's mother was called empress dowager, his chief consort empress, with additional ranks such as beauty, good person, eighth son, and seventh son.

value.zh: 至孝武制婕妤之徒凡十四等。
value.en: Under Emperor Xiaowu the ranks from talented attendant onward reached fourteen grades in all.
value.literal: By Emperor Xiaowu's time the system of ranks including talented attendant and the like totaled fourteen grades.

value.zh: 降及魏、晉，母后之號，皆因漢法；
value.en: Through Wei and Jin, titles for imperial mothers all followed Han precedent;
value.literal: Down through Wei and Jin, titles for imperial mothers all followed Han law;

value.zh: 自夫人以下，世有增損焉。
value.en: below the rank of consort, each age revised the roster.
value.literal: from consort downward, each generation added or reduced ranks.

value.zh: 高祖撥亂反正，深鑒奢逸，惡衣菲食，務先節儉。
value.en: Gaozu ended chaos and restored rule, deeply wary of extravagance, preferring coarse dress and plain fare and putting thrift first.
value.literal: Emperor Gaozu quelled disorder and restored order, taking deep warning from luxury and excess, wearing poor clothes and eating plain food, putting frugality first.

value.zh: 配德早終，長秋曠位，嬪嬙之數，無所改作。
value.en: His worthy partner died young; the empress's seat stayed vacant; the roster of palace women was not revised.
value.literal: His worthy consort died early; the office of empress stood empty; the numbers of palace women were left unchanged.

value.zh: 太宗、世祖出自儲藩，而妃並先殂，又不建椒閫。
value.en: Taizong and Shizu rose from the heir's household, but their consorts died first and neither raised an empress.
value.literal: Emperor Taizong and Emperor Shizu came up from the heir's establishment, yet their consorts all died first, and neither established an empress.

value.zh: 今之撰錄，止備闕云。
value.en: This record therefore fills only the gaps.
value.literal: The present compilation supplies only what is missing.

value.zh: 父穆之，字思靜，晉司空華六世孫。
value.en: Her father Muzhi, styled Sijing, was a sixth-generation descendant of Jin's Minister of Works Hua.
value.literal: Her father Muzhi, styled Sijing, was sixth-generation descendant of Jin Minister of Works Hua.

value.zh: 曾祖輿坐華誅，徙興古，未至召還。
value.en: Her great-grandfather Yu was condemned in Hua's case, exiled toward Xinggu, and recalled before he arrived.
value.literal: Her great-grandfather Yu was implicated in Hua's execution, banished to Xinggu, recalled before he arrived.

value.zh: 及過江，爲丞相掾，太子舍人。
value.en: After crossing south he was a chancellor's aide and a crown prince attendant.
value.literal: After crossing the Yangtze he served as aide to the chancellor and as attendant to the crown prince.

value.zh: 穆之少方雅，有識鑒。
value.en: Muzhi in youth was upright and elegant, with keen judgment.
value.literal: Muzhi in youth was square and refined, with discernment.

value.zh: 宋元嘉中，爲員外散騎侍郎。
value.en: In Song's Yuanjia era he became an outer member of the Scattered Cavalry.
value.literal: In Yuanjia of Song he was made Outer Member of the Scattered Cavalry.

value.zh: 與吏部尚書江湛、太子左率袁淑善，淑薦之於始興王濬，濬深引納焉。
value.en: He was close to Minister of the Civil Service Jiang Zhan and the heir's left leader Yuan Shu; Shu recommended him to Prince Jun of Shixing, and Jun took him in warmly.
value.literal: He was on good terms with Minister of the Civil Service Jiang Zhan and Left Leader of the Heir's Household Yuan Shu; Shu recommended him to Prince Jun of Shixing, and Jun warmly received him.

value.zh: 穆之鑒其禍萌，思違其難，言於湛求外出。
value.en: Muzhi saw trouble brewing and sought a way out; he asked Zhan to post him away.
value.literal: Muzhi saw the disaster sprouting and thought to escape the trouble; he spoke to Zhan asking to be sent out.

value.zh: 湛將用爲東縣，固乞遠郡，久之，得爲寧遠將軍、交阯太守。
value.en: Zhan meant to place him in an eastern county, but he begged for a distant commandery and, after long delay, became General Pacifying the Distance and Administrator of Jiaozhi.
value.literal: Zhan was about to use him in an eastern county; he firmly begged for a distant commandery, and after long delay became General Pacifying the Distance and Administrator of Jiaozhi.

value.zh: 治有異績。
value.en: He governed with outstanding results.
value.literal: His administration showed exceptional achievement.

value.zh: 會刺史死，交土大亂，穆之威懷循拊，境內以寧。
value.en: When the inspector died, Jiaozhi erupted in chaos; Muzhi won men by authority and kindness, and the region grew calm.
value.literal: When the inspector died, Jiaozhi fell into great disorder; Muzhi by awe and kindness guided and comforted them, and within the borders there was peace.

value.zh: 宋文帝聞之嘉焉，將以爲交州刺史，會病卒。
value.en: Emperor Wen of Song heard and praised him and was about to make him Inspector of Jiaozhi, but Muzhi fell ill and died.
value.literal: Emperor Wen of Song heard and praised this, and was about to make him Inspector of Jiaozhi, but Muzhi fell ill and died.

value.zh: 子弘籍，字真藝，齊初爲鎮西參軍，卒於官。
value.en: His son Hongji, styled Zhenyi, in early Qi served as staff officer to the Pacify West army and died in office.
value.literal: His son Hongji, styled Zhenyi, in early Qi was staff officer to the Pacify West army and died in office.

value.zh: 高祖踐阼，追贈穆之光祿大夫，加金章。
value.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Muzhi was posthumously made Glory Grand Master with a gold seal.
value.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, Muzhi was posthumously made Glory Grand Master with gold seal.

value.zh: 又詔曰：「亡舅齊鎮西參軍，素風雅猷，夙肩名輩，降年不永，早世潛輝。
value.en: Another edict said: "My late uncle, Qi's Pacify West staff officer, bore pure taste and fine counsel and long stood among eminent men; his years were short and his light went under early.
value.literal: Another edict said: "The deceased uncle, Qi staff officer to the Pacify West army, had pure style and elegant counsel, from of old shoulder to shoulder with famous men; his years were not long, early leaving the world his light hid.

value.zh: 朕少離苦辛，情地彌切，雖宅相克成，輅車靡贈，興言永往，觸目慟心。
value.en: I knew bitter separation in youth and feel the bond all the more; though tombs were raised, no carriage of gifts went forth, and every thought of his going wrings the heart.
value.literal: I in youth parted from bitter hardship, kin feeling ever keener; though dwelling tombs were mutually accomplished, touring carriage had no gift-offering, words rising at eternal parting, the eye touched brings anguished heart.

value.zh: 可追贈廷尉卿。」
value.en: Let him be posthumously made Minister of Justice."
value.literal: He may be posthumously made Minister of Justice."

value.zh: 弘籍無子，從父弟弘策以第三子纘爲嗣，別有傳。
value.en: Hongji had no son; his cousin Hongce made his third son Zuan the heir—see the separate biography.
value.literal: Hongji had no son; his father's younger brother's son Hongce made his third son Zuan heir—treated in a separate biography.

value.zh: 梁書卷第十九 列傳第十三
value.en: Book of Liang, Volume 19, Biographies 13
value.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 19, Biographies 13

value.zh: 天監初，遷驍騎將軍、領少府卿；
value.en: At Tianjian's opening he was Raiding Cavalry General and palace workshop director;
value.literal: At the start of Tianjian he was promoted to Raiding Cavalry General and Director of the Palace Workshop;

value.zh: 俄遷御史中丞，領本州大中正。
value.en: soon Censor-in-Chief and head of his province's great rectifiers.
value.literal: soon he was Censor-in-Chief and head of the great rectifiers of his native province.

value.zh: 初，藹發江陵，無故於船得八車輻，如中丞健步避道者，至是果遷焉。
value.en: Leaving Jiangling he had found eight carriage hubs on the boat, like a censor stepping aside—and now the omen held.
value.literal: When Ai had set out from Jiangling he found for no reason on the boat eight carriage hubs, like a censor's brisk step giving way on the road—and now the omen came true.

value.zh: 藹性公強，居憲臺甚稱職。
value.en: Fair and forceful, he shone at the censorate.
value.literal: Ai's nature was fair and forceful; at the censorate he filled the post admirably.

value.zh: 時長沙宣武王將葬，而車府忽於庫火油絡，欲推主者。
value.en: King Xuanwu of Changsha was to be buried when the carriage office found lamp oil burning in the storehouse and sought a culprit.
value.literal: At the time King Xuanwu of Changsha was to be buried, and the carriage office suddenly found lamp oil ablaze in the storehouse; they wished to impeach the keeper.

value.zh: 藹曰：「昔晉武庫火，張華以爲積油萬石必然。
value.en: Ai said, "When Jin's arsenal burned, Zhang Hua said ten thousand stone of piled oil made fire inevitable.
value.literal: Ai said: "In Jin, when the arsenal caught fire, Zhang Hua held that ten thousand stone of oil piled up made it inevitable.

value.zh: 今庫若有灰，非吏罪也。」
value.en: If ash lies in the storehouse, no clerk is to blame."
value.literal: If the storehouse now holds ash, it is no clerk's crime."

value.zh: 旣而檢之，果有積灰。
value.en: Inspection found piled ash.
value.literal: On inspection there was indeed piled ash.

value.zh: 時稱其博物弘恕焉。
value.en: The age praised his learning and his large forgiveness.
value.literal: The age praised his broad learning and large forgiveness.

value.zh: 梁書卷第四十 列傳第三十四
value.en: Book of Liang, Volume 40, Biography 34
value.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 40, Biography 34

value.zh: 顯幼而聰敏，當世號曰神童。
value.en: Xian was bright from childhood; men of his day called him a prodigy.
value.literal: Xian was clever from childhood; his contemporaries called him a divine child.

value.zh: 天監初，舉秀才，解褐中軍臨川王行參軍，俄署法曹。
value.en: When Tianjian opened he was presented as a cultivated talent, entered service as staff officer to the Prince of Linchuan in the Central Army, and soon headed the law bureau.
value.literal: At the opening of Tianjian he was recommended as a cultivated talent, relieved his clerk’s collar as Administrative Officer on the staff of the Prince of Linchuan in the Central Army, and soon served as Chief of the Law Bureau.

value.zh: 顯好學，博涉多參通，任昉嘗得一篇缺簡書，文字零落，歷示諸人，莫能識者，顯云是《古文尚書》所刪逸篇，昉檢《周書》，果如其說，昉因大相賞異。
value.en: Xian loved study and ranged across many disciplines; once Ren Fang had a bamboo slip with characters broken and faded, showed it around, and no one could read it—Xian said it was a lost passage cut from the Old Text Documents; Fang checked the Documents of Zhou and found it exact, and from then held him in wonder.
value.literal: Xian loved learning and ranged widely in many fields; once Ren Fang obtained a fragmentary bamboo text with characters scattered and eroded, showed it to everyone, and none could read it—Xian said it was a lost passage deleted from the Old Text Documents, and when Fang checked the Documents of Zhou it matched exactly; Fang was thereafter greatly struck by him.

value.zh: 丁母憂，服闋，尚書令沈約命駕造焉，於坐策顯經史十事，顯對其九。
value.en: After his mother’s mourning, the Director of the Department of State Affairs Shen Yue came by carriage to call on him and, seated, examined him on ten points of canon and history—Xian answered nine.
value.literal: When his mother’s mourning ended, the Director of the Department of State Affairs Shen Yue came in his carriage to visit, and at the seat tested Xian on ten matters from the classics and histories—Xian answered nine.

value.zh: 約曰：「老夫昏忘，不可受策；
value.en: Yue said, “This old man is dim and forgetful; I cannot sit for your test—
value.literal: Yue said: “This old man is muddled and forgetful; I cannot submit to examination—

value.zh: 雖然，聊試數事，不可至十也。」
value.en: Still, try me on a few—you must not make it ten.”
value.literal: Even so, let me try a few things—you must not reach ten.”

value.zh: 顯問其五，約對其二。
value.en: Xian put five questions to him; Yue answered two.
value.literal: Xian questioned him on five; Yue answered two.

value.zh: 陸倕聞之歎曰：「劉郎可謂差人，雖吾家平原詣張壯武，王粲謁伯喈，必無此對。」
value.en: Lu Chui heard and sighed, “Master Liu is a man apart—even when our Lu Ji sought out Zhang Hua, or Wang Can called on Cai Yong, there was never such an exchange.”
value.literal: Lu Chui heard of it and sighed: “One may say Master Liu is a man apart—even when our house’s Lu Ji called on Zhang Hua, or when Wang Can visited Cai Yong, there could not have been such parry and riposte.”

value.zh: 其爲名流推賞如此。
value.en: So the leading men of the age honored him.
value.literal: Such was the esteem in which leading minds held him.

value.zh: 及約爲太子少傅，乃引爲五官掾，俄兼廷尉正。
value.en: When Yue became mentor to the heir apparent, he drew Xian in as aide in the Five Offices; soon Xian also served as director under the Court of Judicial Review.
value.literal: When Yue became Mentor to the Heir Apparent, he brought Xian in as Aide in the Five Offices, and soon he also served as Director under the Court of Judicial Review.

value.zh: 五兵尚書傅昭掌著作，撰國史，引顯爲佐。
value.en: Fu Zhao, Minister of the Five Armies and overseer of historiography, was compiling the national history and took Xian as his assistant.
value.literal: Fu Zhao, Minister of the Five Armies and in charge of historiography, was compiling the national history and brought Xian in as assistant.

value.zh: 九年，始革尚書五都選，顯以本官兼吏部郎，又除司空臨川王外兵參軍，遷尚書儀曹郎。
value.en: In year nine the five selection directorates were first reformed; Xian kept his post while also serving as director in the Ministry of Personnel, was made external military officer to the Minister of Works, the Prince of Linchuan, and then Gentleman of the Ceremonial Bureau.
value.literal: In year nine the Ministry system was first reformed for the five directorates of selection; Xian in his existing post also served as Director in the Ministry of Personnel, was further appointed External Military Officer to the Minister of Works, the Prince of Linchuan, and was transferred to Gentleman of the Ceremonial Bureau.

value.zh: 嘗爲《上朝詩》，沈約見而美之，時約郊居宅新成，因命工書人題之於壁。
value.en: He once wrote a poem on the morning audience; Shen Yue admired it, and when Yue’s suburban house was newly finished he had a scribe brush it on the wall.
value.literal: Once he composed a poem on morning audience; Shen Yue read it with admiration, and at the time Yue’s suburban residence was newly built—he had a scribe paint it on the wall.

value.zh: 出爲臨川王記室參軍。
value.en: He left the capital as recorder to the Prince of Linchuan.
value.literal: He went out as Recorder on the staff of the Prince of Linchuan.

value.zh: 建康平，復入爲尚書儀曹侍郎，兼中書通事舍人。
value.en: After Jiankang was pacified he returned as vice director of ceremonial affairs and again Master of Documents for Palace Affairs.
value.literal: When Jiankang was pacified he returned as Vice Director of Ceremonial Affairs in the Ministry of Rites and concurrently Master of Documents for Palace Affairs.

value.zh: 出爲秣陵令，又除驃騎鄱陽王記室，兼中書舍人，累遷步兵校尉、中書侍郎，舍人如故。
value.en: He served as magistrate of Moling, then recorder to the Prince of Poyang, Cavalry General, again Master of Documents, and rose to Commandant of Footsoldiers and Secretariat gentleman, keeping the palace post throughout.
value.literal: He went out as Magistrate of Moling, was again made Recorder to the Prince of Poyang, Cavalry General, with concurrent service as Master of Documents, and was promoted in succession to Commandant of Footsoldiers and Gentleman of the Secretariat, still Master of Documents.

value.zh: 樂
value.en: Music
value.literal: Music

value.zh: 永明二年，尚書殿中曹奏：「太祖高皇帝廟神室奏《高德宣烈之舞》，未有歌詩，郊應須歌辭。
value.en: In the second year of Yongming, the Secretariat's Director of Palace Affairs reported: 「At Grand Ancestor Gaozu's temple chamber they perform "Dance Proclaiming Lofty Virtue and Martial Glory," but there is no hymn yet; the suburban rite still needs words.
value.literal: In the second year of Yongming, the Director of Palace Affairs in the Secretariat memorialized: 「Grand Ancestor Emperor Gaozu's temple chamber performs "Dance Proclaiming Lofty Virtue and Martial Glory"—no hymn yet; suburban sacrifice needs hymn text.

value.zh: 穆皇后廟神室，亦未有歌辭。
value.en: Empress Mu's temple chamber likewise has no hymn text.
value.literal: Empress Mu's temple chamber likewise has no hymn text yet.

value.zh: 案傅玄云：『登歌廟異其文，饗神七室同辭。』
value.en: On Fu Xuan's view: 『Ascent hymns differ in wording from temple to temple, but the seven chambers share one text for spirit-feasting.』
value.literal: Examining Fu Xuan's statement: 『Ascent hymns differ in text for each temple; feasting-spirit songs use the same wording for all seven chambers.』

value.zh: 此議爲允。
value.en: This view was accepted.
value.literal: This opinion is approved.

value.zh: 又尋漢世歌篇，多少無定，皆稱事立文，竝多八句，然後轉韻。
value.en: Reviewing Han song-cycles shows no fixed length: each was shaped to its subject, usually eight lines before the rhyme turned.
value.literal: Again searching Han-era song chapters, their length was unset; all were titled to the occasion and composed accordingly, mostly eight lines, then rhyme shifted.

value.zh: 時有兩三韻而轉，其例甚寡。
value.en: Occasionally the rhyme shifted after two or three stanzas, but that was rare.
value.literal: At times two or three rhymes would shift; such cases were very few.

value.zh: 張華、夏侯湛亦同前式。
value.en: Zhang Hua and Xiahou Zhan followed the same earlier form.
value.literal: Zhang Hua and Xiahou Zhan likewise followed the earlier pattern.

value.zh: 傅玄改韻頗數，更傷簡節之美。
value.en: Fu Xuan changed rhyme too often, which further marred the grace of compact restraint.
value.literal: Fu Xuan shifted rhyme rather often, further harming the beauty of brevity and rhythm.

value.zh: 近世王韶之、顏延之並四韻乃轉，得賒促之中。
value.en: Recently Wang Shao-zhi and Yan Yan-zhi both turned rhyme after four stanzas, hitting the mean between long and short.
value.literal: In recent times Wang Shao-zhi and Yan Yan-zhi both shifted after four rhymes, achieving a balance between extended and compressed.

value.zh: 顏延之、謝莊作三廟歌，皆各三章章八句，此于序述功業詳略爲宜，今宜依之。
value.en: Yan Yan-zhi and Xie Zhuang wrote hymns for three temples, each in three eight-line chapters—fitting for fuller or briefer accounts of merit—and that pattern should be adopted now.
value.literal: Yan Yan-zhi and Xie Zhuang composed three-temple songs, each with three chapters of eight lines apiece—this suits narrating achievements in greater or lesser detail; it should be followed now.

value.zh: 郊配之日，改降尊作主，禮殊宗廟；
value.en: On suburban-sacrifice days, when the honored one is demoted to preside, the rite differs from ancestral-temple ceremony;
value.literal: On suburban sacrifice days, when the honored is lowered in rank to serve as host, the rite differs from the ancestral temple;

value.zh: 穆后母儀之化，事異經綸。
value.en: Empress Mu's maternal transforming grace is a matter apart from governance.
value.literal: Empress Mu's maternal exemplary transforming influence—the matter differs from statecraft.

value.zh: 此二歌爲一章八句，別奏事御奉行。」
value.en: These two hymns are to be one eight-line chapter each, performed separately as the ceremony requires."
value.literal: These two songs are one chapter of eight lines each; they are to be performed separately as ceremonial officers carry out the rite."

value.zh: 詔「可」。
value.en: The edict said "Granted."
value.literal: An edict read "Approved."

value.zh: 尚書令王儉造太廟二室及郊配辭。
value.en: Wang Jian, Minister Over the Masses, composed hymn texts for two ancestral-temple chambers and the suburban rite.
value.literal: Minister Over the Masses Wang Jian composed hymn texts for two Imperial Ancestral Temple chambers and suburban sacrifice.

value.zh: 元會大饗四廂樂歌辭，晉泰始五年太僕傅玄撰。
value.en: Lyrics for the New Year's Grand Assembly feast in the four galleries, composed by Jin Grand Master of the Household Fu Xuan in the fifth year of Taishi.
value.literal: New Year's grand feast four-gallery music hymn texts, composed in the fifth year of Taishi by Jin Grand Master of the Household Fu Xuan.

value.zh: 正旦大會行禮歌詩四章，壽酒詩一章，食舉東西廂樂十三章，黃門郎張華作。
value.en: For the New Year's Day grand assembly: four ceremonial hymn-poems, one longevity-wine poem, and thirteen food-raising gallery pieces east and west, by Yellow Gate Gentleman Zhang Hua.
value.literal: New Year's Day grand assembly ceremonial hymn-poems four chapters, longevity wine poem one chapter, food-raising east-west gallery music thirteen chapters, Yellow Gate Gentleman Zhang Hua composed.

value.zh: 上壽食舉行禮詩十八章，中書監荀勗、侍郎成公綏，言數各異。
value.en: Eighteen hymn-poems for longevity presentation and food-raising were credited to Secretariat Director Xun Xu and Attendant-in-Ordinary Cheng Gong-sui, but with differing line counts.
value.literal: Longevity presentation and food-raising ceremonial poems eighteen chapters, Secretariat Director Xun Xu and Attendant-in-Ordinary Cheng Gong-sui—the line counts each differ.

value.zh: 宋黃門郎王韶之造《肆夏》四章，行禮一章，上壽一章，登歌三章，食舉十章，《前後舞歌》一章。
value.en: In Song, Yellow Gate Gentleman Wang Shao-zhi composed four "Si Xia" chapters, one ceremonial piece, one longevity presentation, three ascent hymns, ten food-raising pieces, and one "Front and Rear Dance Song."
value.literal: Song Yellow Gate Gentleman Wang Shao-zhi made "Si Xia" four chapters, ceremonial one chapter, longevity presentation one chapter, ascent hymns three chapters, food-raising ten chapters, "Front and Rear Dance Song" one chapter.

value.zh: 齊微改革，多仍舊辭。
value.en: Qi made slight revisions, largely keeping the old wording.
value.literal: Qi slightly reformed, mostly retaining old texts.

value.zh: 其《前後舞》二章新改。
value.en: Its two "Front and Rear Dance" chapters were newly rewritten.
value.literal: Its "Front and Rear Dance" two chapters newly revised.

value.zh: 其臨軒樂，亦奏《肆夏·於鑠》四章。
value.en: For music at the facing-the-gallery audience, four chapters of "Si Xia: Imposing Splendor" were also played.
value.literal: Its facing-the-gallery music also performed "Si Xia: Imposing Splendor" four chapters.

value.zh: 《前舞》、《後舞》，晉泰始九年造。
value.en: "Front Dance" and "Rear Dance"—created in the ninth year of Taishi under Jin.
value.literal: "Front Dance" and "Rear Dance"—created in the ninth year of Taishi under Jin.

value.zh: 《正德大豫舞》，傅玄、張華各爲歌辭。
value.en: "Correct Virtue" and "Great Abundance Dance"—Fu Xuan and Zhang Hua each supplied song words.
value.literal: "Correct Virtue" and "Great Abundance Dance" — Fu Xuan and Zhang Hua each wrote song lyrics.

value.zh: 宋元嘉中，改《正德》爲《前舞》，《大豫》爲《後舞》。
value.en: In Song's Yuanjia reign, "Correct Virtue" became "Front Dance" and "Great Abundance" became "Rear Dance."::
value.literal: In Song's Yuanjia era, "Correct Virtue" was changed to "Front Dance," "Great Abundance" to "Rear Dance."::

value.zh: 虞玩之
value.en: Yu Wanzhi
value.literal: Yu Wanzhi

value.zh: 元徽中，爲右丞。
value.en: In the Yuanhui era he served as right vice director.
value.literal: In the Yuanhui era he served as right vice director.

value.zh: 時太祖參政，與玩之書曰：「張華爲度支尚書，事不徒然。
value.en: At the time the founding sovereign was directing affairs of state and wrote to Wanzhi: "When Zhang Hua served as minister of revenue, his work was not in vain.
value.literal: At the time the founding sovereign held real power in government and wrote to Wanzhi: "When Zhang Hua served as minister of revenue, his work was not in vain.

value.zh: 今漕藏有闕，吾賢居右丞，已覺金粟可積也。」
value.en: Now the transport treasuries show gaps; with you, my worthy, as right vice director, I already sense gold and grain may begin to accumulate."
value.literal: Now the transport treasuries have gaps; with you, my worthy, in the right vice director's post, I already sense that gold and grain may be piled up."

value.zh: 玩之上表陳府庫錢帛，器械役力，所懸轉多，興用漸廣，慮不支歲月。
value.en: Wanzhi memorialized that the palace treasury's cash, silk, equipment, and labor levies were ever more entangled in suspense, new outlays steadily widened, and he feared the year could not be sustained.
value.literal: Wanzhi memorialized on the palace treasury's cash, silk, equipment, and labor levies: what hung in suspense grew ever greater, new outlays steadily widened, and he feared the year could not be sustained.

value.zh: 朝議優報之。
value.en: Court deliberation returned him a favorable reply.
value.literal: Court deliberation gave him a favorable reply.

value.zh: 遷安成王車騎錄事，轉少府。
value.en: He was moved to recorder on the Prince of Ancheng's chariot-and-cavalry staff, then to the lesser treasury.
value.literal: He was moved to recorder on the Prince of Ancheng's chariot-and-cavalry staff, then to the lesser treasury.

value.zh: 梁文獻張皇后 武德郗皇后 武丁貴嬪 武阮修容 簡文王皇后 元徐妃 敬夏太后 敬王皇后 陳武宣章皇后 文沈皇后 廢帝王皇后 宣柳皇后 後主沈皇后
value.en: This chapter treats Empress Zhang Wenxian of Liang, Empress Chi Wude of Liang, Honored Consort Ding, Lady of Cultivated Elegance Ruan, Empress Wang of Emperor Jianwen of Liang, Consort Xu of Emperor Yuan of Liang, Empress Dowager Xia the Reverent, Empress Wang the Reverent, Empress Zhang Xuan of Emperor Wu of Chen, Empress Shen of Emperor Wen of Chen, Empress Wang of the deposed emperor, Empress Liu Xuan of Emperor Xuan of Chen, and Empress Shen of the Chen last ruler.
value.literal: Empress Zhang the Dedicated of Liang, Empress Chi the Martial Virtue of Liang, Honored Consort Ding the Martial of Liang, Lady of Cultivated Elegance Ruan the Martial of Liang, Empress Wang of Emperor Jianwen, Consort Xu of Emperor Yuan, Empress Dowager Xia the Reverent, Empress Wang the Reverent, Empress Zhang the Proclaiming Virtue of Chen Wu, Empress Shen of Emperor Wen, Empress Wang of the Deposed Emperor, Empress Liu the Proclaiming of Emperor Xuan, Empress Shen of the Last Ruler.

value.zh: 穆之字思靜，晉司空華六世孫也。
value.en: Zhang Muzhi, courtesy name Sijing, was a sixth-generation descendant of Zhang Hua, Grand Marshal of Jin.
value.literal: Muzhi, whose courtesy name was Sijing, was a sixth-generation descendant of Zhang Hua, Grand Marshal of Jin.

value.zh: 少方雅，有識鑒。
value.en: In youth he was cultivated and discerning.
value.literal: As a youth he was refined and elegant, with discernment and judgment.

value.zh: 初為員外散騎侍郎，深被始興王浚引納。
value.en: He began as a supernumerary attendant in the outer retinue of cavalries and was warmly taken up by Liu Jun, Prince of Shixing.
value.literal: He first served as Supernumerary Attendant in the Outer Retinue of Cavalries and was deeply drawn in by Prince Jun of Shixing.

value.zh: 穆之鑒其禍萌，求為交址太守，政有異績。
value.en: Muzhi saw the disaster Liu Jun would bring and asked to be sent away as administrator of Jiaozhi, where his rule won unusual praise.
value.literal: Muzhi perceived the budding of disaster in him and requested appointment as Administrator of Jiaozhi; his administration won unusual achievements.

value.zh: 宋文帝將以為交州刺史，會病卒。
value.en: Emperor Wen of Song was on the point of making him inspector of Jiaozhou when Muzhi died of illness.
value.literal: Emperor Wen of Song was about to appoint him Inspector of Jiaozhou when Muzhi died of illness.

value.zh: 子弘籍字真藝，齊初為鎮西參軍，卒於官。
value.en: His son Zhang Hongji, courtesy name Zhenyi, served in early Qi as staff officer to the army pacifying the west and died in that post.
value.literal: His son Hongji, courtesy name Zhenyi, in the early Qi served as Staff Officer for the Army of Pacifying the West and died in office.

value.zh: 梁武踐阼，追贈穆之光祿大夫，加金章紫綬。
value.en: When Emperor Wu of Liang took the throne, he posthumously granted Muzhi the office of grand master of the palace with the golden seal and purple cord.
value.literal: When Liang Wu took the throne, he posthumously granted Muzhi the office of Grand Master of the Palace with the Golden Seal and Purple Cord.

value.zh: 贈弘籍廷尉卿。
value.en: He also posthumously granted Hongji the office of minister of justice.
value.literal: He posthumously granted Hongji the office of Minister of Justice.

value.zh: 弘籍無子，從父弟弘策以子纘嗣，別有傳。
value.en: Hongji had no sons; his younger cousin Zhang Hongce had his own son Zuan continue the line — a separate biography treats them.
value.literal: Hongji had no sons; his collateral younger cousin Hongce had his son Zuan succeed to the line — treated separately in another biography.

value.zh: 荀伯玉
value.en: Xun Boyu
value.literal: Xun Boyu

value.zh: 元徽中，為尚書右丞。
value.en: In Yuanhui he was Right Assistant Minister of the Secretariat.
value.literal: In Yuanhui he was Right Assistant Minister of the Secretariat.

value.zh: 齊高帝參政，與玩之書曰：「張華為度支尚書，事不徒然。
value.en: When Emperor Gao of Qi assisted in government he wrote to Wanzhi, "Zhang Hua as Minister of Revenue—the affair was not in vain.
value.literal: When the Qi Emperor Gao assisted in government he wrote to Wanzhi: "Zhang Hua as Minister of Revenue—the affair was not in vain.

value.zh: 今漕藏有闕，吾賢居右丞，已覺金粟可積也。」
value.en: Now the transport stores have gaps; my worthy man holds the right assistant post—I already feel gold and grain can be accumulated."
value.literal: Now the transport stores have gaps; my worthy man holds the right assistant post—I already feel gold and grain can be accumulated."

value.zh: 玩之上表，陳府庫錢帛，器械役力，所懸轉多，興用漸廣，慮不支歲月。
value.en: Wanzhi submitted a memorial stating that the headquarters' cash, silk, implements, labor, and suspended items grew ever more, expenditures gradually widened, and he feared they would not last the year.
value.literal: Wanzhi submitted a memorial stating that the headquarters' cash, silk, implements, labor, and suspended items grew ever more, expenditures gradually widened, and he feared they would not last the year.

value.zh: 朝議優報之。
value.en: Court discussion favorably replied.
value.literal: Court discussion favorably replied.

value.zh: 高帝鎮東府，朝廷致敬，玩之為少府，猶躡屐造席。
value.en: When Emperor Gao garrisoned the Eastern Headquarters, the court showed respect; Wanzhi was Minister of the Privy Purse and still wore clogs to take his seat.
value.literal: When the Emperor Gao garrisoned the Eastern Headquarters, the court showed respect; Wanzhi was Minister of the Privy Purse and still wore clogs to take his seat.

value.zh: 高帝取屐親視之，訛黑斜銳，蒵斷以芒接之。
value.en: Emperor Gao took the clog and examined it personally—worn black, slanting and sharp, the rush broken and joined with awn.
value.literal: The Emperor Gao took the clog and examined it personally—worn black, slanting and sharp, the rush broken and joined with awn.

value.zh: 問曰：「卿此屐已幾載？」
value.en: He asked, "How many years have you worn these clogs?"
value.literal: He asked: "How many years have you worn these clogs?"

value.zh: 玩之曰：「初釋褐拜征北行佐買之，著已三十年，貧士竟不辦易。」
value.en: Wanzhi said, "When I first left the cloth and was appointed Northern Expedition traveling staff officer I bought them; I have worn them thirty years—a poor gentleman truly cannot afford to replace them."
value.literal: Wanzhi said: "When I first left the cloth and was appointed Northern Expedition traveling staff officer I bought them; I have worn them thirty years—a poor gentleman truly cannot afford to replace them."

value.zh: 高帝咨嗟，因賜以新屐。
value.en: Emperor Gao sighed in admiration and bestowed new clogs.
value.literal: The Emperor Gao sighed in admiration and bestowed new clogs.

value.zh: 玩之不受。
value.en: Wanzhi did not accept them.
value.literal: Wanzhi did not accept them.

value.zh: 帝問其故，答曰：「今日之賜，恩華俱重，但蓍簪弊席，復不可遺，所以不敢當。」
value.en: The emperor asked the reason; he replied, "Today's gift—favor and splendor together are weighty; but worn rush hairpin and broken mat cannot be discarded, so I dare not accept."
value.literal: The Emperor asked the reason; he replied: "Today's gift—favor and splendor together are weighty; but worn rush hairpin and broken mat cannot be discarded, so I dare not accept."

value.zh: 帝善之。
value.en: The emperor approved.
value.literal: The Emperor approved.

value.zh: 拜驃騎諮議參軍。
value.en: He was appointed Valiant Cavalry Adviser.
value.literal: He was appointed Valiant Cavalry Adviser.

value.zh: 霸府初開，賓客輻湊，高帝留意簡接。
value.en: When the Hegemon's headquarters first opened, guests gathered in crowds; Emperor Gao paid attention to selective reception.
value.literal: When the Hegemon's headquarters first opened, guests gathered in crowds; the Emperor Gao paid attention to selective reception.

value.zh: 玩之與樂安任遐俱以應對有席上之美，齊名見遇。
value.en: Wanzhi and Ren Xia of Le'an together had beauty in banquet repartee and were equally famed and favored.
value.literal: Wanzhi and Ren Xia of Le'an together had beauty in banquet repartee and were equally famed and favored.

value.zh: 玩之遷黃門郎。
value.en: Wanzhi was transferred to Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
value.literal: Wanzhi was transferred to Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

value.zh: 先時，宋世人籍欺巧，及高帝即位，敕玩之與驍騎將軍傅堅意檢定之。
value.en: Previously, under Song, people practiced fraud and trickery in the household registers. When Emperor Gao ascended the throne, he ordered Wanzhi and General of Agile Cavalry Fu Jianyi to inspect and settle them.
value.literal: Previously, under Song, people practiced fraud and trickery in the household registers; when Emperor Gao ascended the throne, he ordered Wanzhi and General of Agile Cavalry Fu Jianyi to inspect and settle them.

value.zh: 建元二年，詔朝臣曰：「黃籍人之大綱，國之政端。
value.en: In the second year of Jianyuan (480), an edict addressed the court ministers, saying, "The yellow registers are the great framework of the people and the foundation of state governance.
value.literal: In the second year of Jianyuan, an edict addressed the court ministers, saying, "The yellow registers are the great framework of the people and the beginning point of the state's governance.
